AMGR-001.description: Implement a SessionSearch tool call that replaces scripts/session-search.sh and scripts/session-search-skill.md with a native Rust implementation. Re-uses the existing persistence layer (MessageStore, HistoryStore, BlobStore) to provide search_history, show_session, recent_sessions, and context_search actions. This tool will also be used by an upcoming compaction refactor to access conversation history programmatically. Agent orchestration (spawn/close/list/message/DeepSearch) is deferred to a separate future AgentManager card.

examples.text: Agent calls SessionSearch(action='recent', count=5) and gets back 5 sessions with name, work unit ID, first/last user message previews, timestamps, message count, project path — enough to triage which session to dig into

Agent calls SessionSearch(action='search', query='RLM-001', context_turns=3) and gets back matches across all content (user inputs, assistant responses, tool calls) with 3 surrounding turns of context per match, grouped by session

Agent calls SessionSearch(action='show') with no session_id and gets back the current session's full conversation with blob-resolved content and reassembled streaming chunks, each message truncated at 5000 chars
Agent calls SessionSearch(action='search', query='DeepSearch', last_hours=24, all_projects=true) and gets back matches from all projects in the last 24 hours, not just the current project
Agent calls SessionSearch(action='search', query='authentication') and gets no matches — tool returns 'No matches found' as structured result, not an error

questions.answer: Split. SessionSearch is its own tool (AMGR-001). Agent orchestration (spawn/close/list/message/DeepSearch) becomes a separate future card.
questions.text: @human: Should AgentManager be one tool with action dispatch, or split into 2-3 separate tools (SessionSearch + AgentSpawn + AgentMessage)? Single tool is simpler for LLM discovery but mixed concerns.

rules.text: Session search must use the existing Rust persistence layer (MessageStore, HistoryStore, BlobStore) — no subprocess to Python or bash
Session search replaces scripts/session-search.sh and scripts/session-search-skill.md entirely — these files become deprecated
Split. SessionSearch is its own tool (AMGR-001). Agent orchestration (spawn/close/list/message/DeepSearch) becomes a separate future card.
SessionSearch output must be usable programmatically (structured data) — not just formatted text — to support compaction and other internal consumers
Streaming chunk reassembly (porting the Python logic from session-search.sh) must reconstruct readable text from [Thinking:...], [Tool:...], and raw SSE fragments
search_history searches ALL persisted content — user inputs, assistant responses, tool calls, tool results, thinking chunks — not just user input history
Search matching uses the ripgrep libraries (grep-regex, grep-searcher, grep-matcher) already bundled in codelet/tools — same engine as the Grep tool
Search defaults to current project sessions only, with an optional flag to search across all projects
Search results include all available metadata per match — session ID, session name, timestamp, role, turn index, matched content preview, surrounding context, project path, provider, message count
Time filtering supports both absolute (after/before ISO timestamps) and relative (last_hours/last_days) parameters — whichever is easiest for the LLM to express in the moment
show_session truncates individual messages at 5000 chars (matching existing tool output conventions), with optional user_only filter and max_turns limit

Three actions: search (keyword search with configurable context_turns around matches), show (load specific session by ID), recent (list recent sessions for discovery) — context_search merged into search as a parameter
All actions have sensible defaults with optional overrides — search defaults to limit=20 matches, recent defaults to count=10, show defaults to all turns with 5000 char truncation per message

SessionSearch replaces the step-by-step Bash workflow from session-search-skill.md (recent → search → show → drill deeper) — the agent follows the same iterative pattern but via native tool calls instead of Bash subprocess

recent action returns: session name, work unit ID (if attached), first/last user message previews, timestamps, message count, and project path — optimized for the LLM to triage which session is relevant
show action defaults to current session if no session_id is provided — 'current' is also accepted as an explicit keyword. The tool resolves it internally via its session_id constructor parameter.
Error handling is simple and direct — empty results return 'No matches found', non-existent session IDs return an error, no suggestion engine or fallback heuristics

AMGR-007.description: Implement an AgentManager tool that allows AI agents to spawn subordinate sessions, manage their lifecycle, send messages between sessions, and set roles. The spawner is always the supervisor — they own the subordinate's lifecycle and close it when done. Spawned sessions are regular agent_loop sessions (not the old supervisor_agent_loop). Subordinates use SessionSearch to pull context from their supervisor when needed, and message to push results back or interrupt. Any session can have a role set (a string acting as system prompt overlay). The old supervisor_agent_loop, ObservationBuffer, automatic observation/injection pipeline, /supervisor command, and supervisor TUI management screens are removed.

examples.text: Supervisor calls AgentManager(action='spawn', role='You are a security reviewer. Analyze code for vulnerabilities, injection risks, and auth bypass.') → returns { session_id: 'uuid' }. Then sends a message with the actual task.

Supervisor spawns a worker, then sends AgentManager(action='message', session_id='worker-id', message='Review src/auth/ for SQL injection vulnerabilities and report back'). The worker receives this as its first prompt and starts working.

Subordinate finishes its task and calls AgentManager(action='message', session_id='supervisor-id', message='Found 2 SQL injection vulnerabilities in query_builder.rs lines 45 and 89. See my analysis.') to report results back.

Subordinate needs context from supervisor — calls SessionSearch(action='show', session_id='supervisor-id', max_turns=10) to see what the supervisor is working on, then adjusts its own work accordingly.

Supervisor calls AgentManager(action='set_role', session_id='my-session-id', role='You are a senior engineer focused on performance optimization') — sets a role on its own session as a system prompt overlay.
User types /role in the TUI — a dialog pops up to enter a role string for the current session. This is the TUI equivalent of AgentManager(action='set_role').
Supervisor is done with a worker — calls AgentManager(action='close', session_id='worker-id') to terminate it and clean up.

Supervisor spawns 3 workers for parallel tasks — a security reviewer, a test writer, and a documentation updater. Each gets a role and a message with their specific task. Supervisor polls them via list/get_status and collects results via messages.

Worker subordinate discovers something urgent — calls AgentManager(action='message', session_id='supervisor-id', message='URGENT: The database migration will drop the users table. Stop the deploy.') to interrupt the supervisor.

rules.text: AgentManager is a single tool with action dispatch — spawn, list, message, set_role, close, get_status — same pattern as SessionSearch and Bridge
The spawner is always the supervisor — they own the subordinate's lifecycle and are responsible for closing it when done
spawn creates a new subordinate session running a regular agent_loop — NOT the old supervisor_agent_loop. Every spawned session is a normal session.
spawn accepts an optional role (string — system prompt overlay for the subordinate). The subordinate always starts idle and waits for a message from the supervisor to begin work.
The spawned subordinate inherits the supervisor's model automatically — no model parameter on spawn

A role is a string that acts as a system prompt overlay for a session — any session can have a role, not just spawned ones. set_role changes the role on any session. In the TUI, /role opens a dialog to set the role on the current session.
Subordinates use SessionSearch to pull context from their supervisor when they need it — no automatic streaming of observations. Context is pulled, not pushed.
Subordinates use the message action to send results back to the supervisor or to interrupt the supervisor when needed
message works between any two sessions — supervisor to subordinate, subordinate to supervisor, or between any two sessions that know each other's IDs. Any-to-any.
close terminates a subordinate session — only the spawner (supervisor) or the user can close it. Close cleans up the parent-child ownership relationship.

The old supervisor_agent_loop, ObservationBuffer, automatic observation/injection pipeline, broadcast subscription for observation, breakpoint detection — all removed. These are replaced by explicit pull (SessionSearch) and push (message) patterns.

The /supervisor TUI command and supervisor management screens (SupervisorTemplateList, SupervisorCreateView, SupervisorTemplateForm) are removed. Replaced by /role command (opens a role dialog for the current session) and AgentManager tool for spawning/managing subordinates.
All actions return JSON. On error: { error: true, code: 'session_not_found' | 'permission_denied' | 'invalid_parameter' | 'delivery_failed', message: string }

message supports an optional context array of session history references — specific turns, turn ranges, or search queries. Resolved at send time so the receiver gets self-contained content. Graceful degradation for missing sessions and zero-match queries.

Resolved message context uses XML-style format: <agent-message from="session-id" role="role"> wraps delivery, <quoted-context> with <from session="id" turns="N-M"> blocks for referenced history. Warnings inline for missing sessions or zero-match queries.
Messages queue in an mpsc channel (capacity 16). No interruption of LLM generation — message waits and is picked up on next iteration. delivery_failed error when channel is full.

The tool module lives at codelet/tools/src/ and is registered in all providers' create_rig_agent() alongside SessionSearch and DeepSearch. AgentManager and SessionSearch are independent — neither imports the other.

AMGR-009.description: Implement the AgentManager tool module with handler-delegated pattern and the core lifecycle actions: spawn (create subordinate session with optional role), list (all sessions with relationships), get_status (detailed session info), close (terminate subordinate, spawner-only). Spawned sessions run regular agent_loop. Spawn inherits supervisor's model. Registered in all providers.

examples.text: Agent calls AgentManager(action='spawn') with no role — gets back { session_id: 'uuid' }. Subordinate inherits the spawner's model and starts idle.
Agent calls AgentManager(action='spawn', role='You are a security reviewer') — gets back { session_id: 'uuid' }. Subordinate has the role set as system prompt overlay.
Agent calls AgentManager(action='list') — returns { sessions: [...] } with all active sessions showing their session_id, name, role, status, spawner_id, subordinate_ids.

Agent calls AgentManager(action='get_status', session_id='valid-uuid') — returns full status object. Agent calls with session_id='nonexistent' — returns { error: true, code: 'session_not_found', message: '...' }.
Spawner agent calls AgentManager(action='close', session_id='subordinate-uuid') — returns { closed: true, session_id: '...' }. ChainOfCommand is cleaned up, session is destroyed.
Non-spawner agent calls AgentManager(action='close', session_id='other-session') — returns { error: true, code: 'permission_denied', message: '...' }. Only the spawner can close.
Agent calls AgentManager(action='spawn') 3 times — creates 3 subordinate workers. Agent calls list — sees all 3 with spawner_id pointing back to the agent's session.
Agent calls AgentManager(action='invalid_action') — returns { error: true, code: 'invalid_parameter', message: 'Unknown action: invalid_action' }.

rules.text: AgentManagerTool follows the handler-delegated pattern: tool struct in codelet-tools with static HashMap<Uuid, Handler>, handler closure created in codelet-napi with persistence access
spawn action creates a new subordinate BackgroundSession running regular agent_loop, inherits the spawner's model, registers relationship in ChainOfCommand via add_supervisor()
spawn accepts an optional role string (system prompt overlay). The subordinate starts idle and waits for a message — no initial prompt is sent
list action returns all sessions with their session_id, name, role, status, spawner_id, and subordinate_ids — no access control

get_status action takes a session_id and returns detailed info: session_id, role, status, model, spawner_id, subordinate_ids, pending_messages. Returns error with code session_not_found if ID is invalid.

close action takes a session_id and terminates the subordinate. Only the spawner (supervisor) can close a session — returns error with code permission_denied otherwise. Cleans up ChainOfCommand relationships.
All actions return JSON. Error responses use shape: { error: true, code: string, message: string }. Error codes: session_not_found, permission_denied, invalid_parameter
The tool is registered in all 5 providers' create_rig_agent() with .tool(AgentManagerTool::new(session_id)) alongside SessionSearch and DeepSearch
Handler is registered in agent_loop() before run via set_agent_manager_handler(session_id, Some(handler)) and cleaned up after via set_agent_manager_handler(session_id, None)
Actions use serde tagged dispatch: #[serde(tag = "action", rename_all = "snake_case")] on AgentManagerAction enum

Messages are delivered through the target session's existing incoming_message channel (mpsc, capacity 16) — reuses the IncomingMessage infrastructure
Messages queue if the target is mid-generation — no interruption of LLM processing. Picked up on next agent_loop iteration via tokio::select!
If the incoming_message channel is full (16 pending messages), the send fails with error code delivery_failed
Message action requires both session_id (target) and message (text content) parameters. Missing either returns error code invalid_parameter
Success response shape: { delivered: true, session_id: 'target-id' }. Error response shape: { error: true, code: string, message: string }
The message is delivered as an IncomingMessage with source_session_id set to the sender's session ID and role_name set to the sender's role (or empty if no role)

Context resolution logic lives in agent_manager_handler.rs as a new resolve_context() function. It uses persistence::load_session() and persistence::get_session_messages_full() — the same persistence layer as SessionSearch. For the search query variant, reuse grep-regex matching (same engine as SessionSearch's handle_search).

The resolved context is prepended to the IncomingMessage.message field before delivery — the existing receive_incoming_message() API stays unchanged. The message body sent to the channel is: sender's text + \n\n<quoted-context>...</quoted-context>. The entire message including resolved context goes through the existing format_incoming_message() pipeline.

When context is provided: use MessageDeliveredWithContext { delivered: true, session_id, context_resolved }. When context is omitted: use existing MessageDelivered { delivered: true, session_id } for backward compat.

AMGR-011.description: Extend the message action to support an optional context array of session history references. Three variants: specific turns, turn ranges, search queries. Resolved at send time using SessionSearch persistence layer. Graceful degradation for missing sessions and zero-match queries. XML-style format for resolved context blocks.

examples.text: Agent sends message with context=[{session_id: 'supervisor-id', turns: [1, 2]}] — receiver gets the message text plus <quoted-context><from session="supervisor-id" turns="1-2">[1] user: ...[2] assistant: ...</from></quoted-context>
Agent sends message with context=[{session_id: 'worker-id', start_turn: 0, end_turn: 5}] — receiver gets turns 0 through 5 from the worker's session history inline with the message
Agent sends message with context=[{session_id: 'peer-id', query: 'SQL injection'}] — receiver gets matching turns from the peer's session containing 'SQL injection' references
Agent sends message referencing a session that was deleted — gets { delivered: true, context_resolved: 0 } and the receiver sees a warning in the quoted-context block

Agent sends message with context=[{session_id: 'worker-id', query: 'nonexistent phrase'}] — query matches nothing, receiver sees '⚠ No matches for query' in the quoted block, but the sender's message text is still delivered

Agent sends message with mixed context array — [{session_id: 'A', turns: [3]}, {session_id: 'B', query: 'auth'}] — both references are resolved and appear as separate <from> blocks inside a single <quoted-context>
Agent sends message without context (or context=[]) — behaves exactly like AMGR-010 plain text delivery, response has no context_resolved field

rules.text: The message action accepts an optional context array alongside the existing session_id and message parameters. Each element is a context reference object.

Three context reference variants are supported: (1) specific turns { session_id, turns: [42,43,44] }, (2) turn range { session_id, start_turn: 10, end_turn: 15 }, (3) search query { session_id, query: 'SQL injection' }. All three can be mixed in a single context array.

Context references are resolved at send time in the handler — the persistence layer (load_session, get_session_messages_full) is accessed to fetch actual message content. Resolved content is appended after the sender's message text before delivery.

Resolved context is formatted in XML-style blocks: <quoted-context><from session="id" turns="N-M">[N] role: content\n[N+1] role: content</from></quoted-context>. Each reference becomes a separate <from> block inside the <quoted-context> wrapper.

Graceful degradation for errors: if a referenced session doesn't exist, the <from> block contains a warning '⚠ Session {id} not found' but the message still delivers. If a search query matches nothing, the block contains '⚠ No matches for query "{term}"'. The sender's message text is always delivered regardless of resolution failures.

The MessageDelivered response includes a context_resolved count: { delivered: true, session_id: 'target', context_resolved: 2 }. This tells the sender how many context references were successfully resolved (vs. degraded with warnings).
When context is omitted or empty, the message action behaves identically to AMGR-010 — plain text delivery with no context resolution. This is backward compatible.

Turn indices are 0-based, matching the position in the session's ordered message list (same indexing as SessionSearch show). Out-of-range turn indices are silently skipped — if turns [1, 999] are requested and the session only has 5 messages, only turn 1 is included.

Blob references in resolved messages are transparently resolved — if a message's content contains a blob:sha256: reference, it's fetched from BlobStore and the actual text content is used in the quoted context.

BOARD-006.description:
The TUI board displays column divider characters in separator lines that should only have them on one side or not at all. Need to distinguish between three separator types:

1. NO COLUMNS (full-width sections):
   - Line ABOVE Git Stashes: ├─────────┤ (no columns above or below)
   - Line BETWEEN Git Stashes and Changed Files: ├─────────┤ (no columns above or below)
   
2. TRANSITION TO COLUMNS (from full-width to columnar):
   - Line BETWEEN Changed Files and Kanban board: ├────┬────┬────┤ (no columns above, columns below)
   
3. COLUMNS (Kanban board section):
   - Lines within Kanban board: ├────┼────┼────┤ (columns above and below)
   
4. TRANSITION FROM COLUMNS (from columnar to full-width):
   - Line BETWEEN Kanban board and key mapping footer: ├────┴────┴────┤ (columns above, no columns below)
   - Line BELOW key mapping footer: └────────────┘ (terminal edge)

Current bug: All separators use column dividers (┼) regardless of context. Need to use ┬ (top junction), ┼ (cross junction), ┴ (bottom junction), or plain ─ (horizontal) based on what's above and below each line.

Line 252 currently shows ├──┼──┤ but should show ├──┴──┴──┤ (bottom junctions where Kanban columns end)

Bottom border should show └────────┘ with NO column dividers (plain horizontal only)

Footer text '← → Columns | ↑↓ jk Work Units | ↵ Details | ESC Back' should have equal padding on left and right to center it
Footer should display '← → Columns ◆ ↑↓ jk Work Units ◆ ↵ Details ◆ ESC Back' with diamond separators

BRIDGE-001.description:
Create a Bridge Rig Tool that the AI agent can call to connect sessions to external WebSocket endpoints.

**This is a RIG TOOL like WebSearch, Read, Bash - NOT NAPI bindings!**

**Tool Location:** `codelet/tools/src/bridge.rs`

**Tool Actions (like WebSearch):**
- `connect` - Connect to a WebSocket endpoint URL
- `disconnect` - Disconnect from a specific endpoint
- `list` - List active bridge connections with status

**How it works:**
1. Agent calls `Bridge` tool with action `connect` and URL
2. Bridge subscribes to session's `watcher_broadcast` channel
3. Bridge connects as WebSocket client to the endpoint
4. Outbound: StreamChunks are serialized to JSON and sent to endpoint
5. Inbound: Messages from endpoint are injected into session's input channel

**Integration:**
- Uses existing `subscribe_to_stream()` from WATCH-003
- Uses existing `watcher_input_tx` for input injection from WATCH-006
- Tool manages global connection state (like WebSearch's browser state)

**Message Format:**
- Outbound: `{"type": "chunk", "session_id": "...", "data": <StreamChunk>}`
- Inbound: `{"type": "input", "session_id": "...", "message": "..."}`

examples.text: Agent calls Bridge(action: 'connect', url: 'ws://localhost:8080') → Returns 'Connected to ws://localhost:8080'
Agent calls Bridge(action: 'connect', url: 'ws://invalid:9999') → Returns error 'Connection refused'
Agent calls Bridge(action: 'list') → Returns '[{url: ws://localhost:8080, state: connected, buffered: 0}]'
Agent calls Bridge(action: 'disconnect', url: 'ws://localhost:8080') → Returns 'Disconnected from ws://localhost:8080'
Agent connects to two endpoints → Both receive all StreamChunks as JSON messages
Endpoint sends {type: 'input', session_id: '...', message: 'build the app'} → Agent receives 'build the app' as user input
Connection drops → Bridge buffers messages, reconnects → Buffered messages delivered to endpoint
Agent calls Bridge(action: 'list') during reconnect → Returns '[{url: ws://localhost:8080, state: reconnecting, buffered: 5}]'

disconnect action: closes WebSocket connection, stops relaying, returns confirmation

Multiple bridges can connect to same session simultaneously (agent calls connect multiple times)

Outbound messages: JSON envelope {type: 'chunk', session_id, data: StreamChunk}
Inbound messages: JSON envelope {type: 'input', session_id, message: string} - injected into session's input channel

BRIDGE-002.description:
Create a standalone TypeScript WebSocket endpoint that bridges codelet sessions to Telegram via BotFather Bot API.

**Location:** `bridge/telegram-endpoint.ts` (single file)

**Architecture:**
1. WebSocket server that codelet's BridgeManager connects to
2. Receives raw StreamChunks (text, thinking, tool_call, tool_result, done, error)
3. Formats and truncates messages for Telegram's 4096 char limit
4. Sends to Telegram chat via Bot API
5. Receives Telegram messages and sends back to codelet as input

**Message Flow:**
- Inbound from codelet: `{type: 'chunk', session_id, data: StreamChunk}`
- Outbound to codelet: `{type: 'input', session_id, message: string}`

**Telegram Integration:**
- Uses `node-telegram-bot-api` npm package
- Bot token from BotFather stored in `.env` file
- Supports MarkdownV2 formatting for code blocks
- Handles message chunking for long responses

**Key Features:**
- Smart truncation (preserve beginning and end)
- Code block preservation with syntax markers
- Thinking content formatted with 💭 prefix
- Tool outputs show tool name and truncated result
- Chat session tracking (which Telegram chat to send to)

CURRENT STATE: telegram-endpoint.ts has simple idle-based buffering (800ms idle or 3500 char limit triggers flush). NO content-aware boundary detection exists yet.
CURRENT STATE: truncateMessage() in telegram-formatting.ts handles oversized messages by preserving first/last 1500 chars with omission indicator. Properly handles code block fence boundaries.
CURRENT STATE: formatForTelegram() passes thinking blocks and tool results verbatim with emoji prefixes (💭, 🔧, ❌). NO summarization exists yet.

NEW: Add findTableBoundary() function to detect markdown tables (lines starting with |). Table boundary takes priority equal to code_block (5). Must detect table header, separator row (|---|), and data rows as a unit.
Use a boundary detector with priority: code_block=table > heading > paragraph > list > sentence > max_size (tables have same priority as code blocks - both are atomic content units)

BRIDGE-006.description: Enhance the Telegram bridge with content-aware chunking that respects natural content boundaries. Currently, telegram-endpoint.ts uses simple idle-based buffering (800ms/3500 chars) that can break messages mid-sentence. This story adds: (1) Boundary detection - flush at sentences, paragraphs, headings, code blocks instead of arbitrary limits, (2) Content summarization - condense thinking blocks to indicators like '🤔 Analyzing...' and tool output to summaries like '📄 Read file.ts (245 lines)', (3) Markdown validation - ensure each chunk has balanced markers before sending.

examples.text: When Claude streams 'I will analyze this...' the full sentence arrives in one message, not 'I will ana' then 'lyze this...'
When Claude outputs a 50-line code block, Telegram receives it as a single message with proper ```language``` formatting
When Claude reads a 500-line file, Telegram shows '📄 Read src/auth.ts (500 lines)' instead of the full file content
When a message would be 5000 chars, it splits at the paragraph break before 4096 chars, sending two complete messages
When Claude writes '## Problem\n\nThe issue is...' the heading starts a new message, not appearing mid-chunk
When a tool call is made, Telegram shows '🔧 Running: Fspec(create-story) with args...' in a formatted way
When there's a list with 10 items, all 10 items arrive together, not split across messages
When Claude outputs a 10-row markdown table, all rows arrive together in one message, preserving the | Date | Price | Change | structure
When a table would exceed 4096 chars, it is split BEFORE the table starts (at paragraph boundary), not mid-table
When Claude starts thinking, Telegram receives '<think>' then the actual thinking content streams naturally, then '</think>' when thinking ends
When multiple thinking chunks arrive in succession, they flow as continuous content between the single <think> and </think> tags - NOT multiple separate '🤔' messages

questions.answer: Truncate with indicator - current truncateMessage() already does this well: keeps first/last 1500 chars with '[...N chars omitted...]' in middle. Properly closes/reopens code block fences.
questions.text: How should images referenced in responses be handled - send the full base64 or just a placeholder?

questions.answer: Yes - tool errors already get ❌ prefix in formatForTelegram(). Keep this pattern.
questions.text: Should there be a configurable 'verbosity level' so users can choose between summary vs detailed output?

rules.text: Messages must never break mid-sentence - chunks should end at sentence boundaries (., !, ?) when possible
Code blocks (``` ... ```) must be sent as complete units, never split across messages
Tool output (especially file reads) should be summarized with key info, not sent verbatim - e.g., '📄 Read file.ts (245 lines)'
Each message must have valid, complete markdown - no unclosed backticks, bold markers, etc.
Messages must respect Telegram's 4096 character limit - split at nearest logical boundary before limit
Paragraph breaks (double newlines) are preferred chunking points
Headings (# ## ###) should start new chunks, not appear mid-chunk
Base64 images are too large for Telegram (4096 char limit). Show placeholder like '📷 [image referenced]' or skip entirely. Current code already handles photo uploads separately.
Markdown tables (| delimited rows) must be sent as complete units - never split mid-row or between header and data rows
Thinking blocks should be streamed with content wrapped in <think>...</think> tags - first thinking chunk gets <think> prefix, last gets </think> suffix, content flows naturally between

TS GlobalSessionStreamManager.handleChunk(sessionId, chunk): Look up handlers for sessionId in sessionHandlers Map, invoke only those. Session isolation via Map lookup, not Rust gating.
TS: DELETE all imports/usages of sessionAttach, sessionDetach from @sengac/codelet-napi. Search entire codebase for these and remove.

BRIDGE-012.description: Replace per-session attach/detach pattern with a single global callback. Rust becomes a pure emitter with zero knowledge of active/attached sessions. TypeScript receives (session_id, chunk) for ALL chunks from ALL sessions and owns all routing logic. Remove ALL deprecated attachment code from Rust - no is_attached flag, no attached_callback, no per-session attach()/detach() methods, no session_attach/session_detach NAPI functions. Clean migration with no fallbacks or comments about the old system.

examples.text: TypeScript calls sessionSetGlobalChunkCallback(cb) at startup. Rust stores cb globally. When any session emits, Rust calls cb(session_id, chunk).

rules.text: Rust exposes ONE global callback via NAPI: sessionSetGlobalChunkCallback(callback). Registered once at TypeScript app startup.
Global callback signature: (session_id: string, chunk: StreamChunk) => void. ALL chunks from ALL sessions go through this ONE callback.
Rust is a pure emitter - ZERO knowledge of which session is active/attached/viewed. No attachment state whatsoever.
TypeScript owns ALL routing logic. GlobalSessionStreamManager dispatches chunks to session-specific handlers based on session_id.
TUI filters by session_id - only displays chunks for the currently-viewed session, ignores chunks from other sessions.
Bridge tool filters by session_id - only relays chunks for the session it's bridged to (session_id comes from tool call context).

REMOVE from Rust: is_attached field, attached_callback field, is_attached() method, attach() method, detach() method, session_attach NAPI, session_detach NAPI. No comments about old system, no fallbacks.

architectureNotes.text:
Standalone TypeScript file at bridge/relay-endpoint.ts with two WebSocket connections: (1) relay-client WS that connects TO the relay server, (2) local WS server that accepts codelet BridgeTool connections.

ONE UNIFIED COMMAND EXECUTION PATH:
ALL messages (input, control, command, chunk, connected) flow through the bridge WebSocket ↔ codelet bridge_relay.rs using the InboundMessage/OutboundMessage/StreamChunk event system. The relay endpoint is a PURE PROTOCOL TRANSLATOR — it translates relay protocol format (camelCase, {data:{}} envelope) to fspec flat InboundMessage format and vice versa. It does NOT call fspecCallback directly.

COMMAND FLOW:
1. Relay sends {type:command, session_id, request_id, data:{command, args}} to relay endpoint
2. Relay endpoint translates to InboundMessage {type:'command', session_id, request_id, command, args_json} and forwards to codelet bridge WS
3. bridge_relay.rs receives 'command' InboundMessage and emits FspecCommandRequest StreamChunk into the session
4. GlobalSessionStreamManager intercepts FspecCommandRequest, calls fspecCallback (same path as LLM Fspec tool)
5. FspecCommandResult StreamChunk flows back through session broadcast channel
6. bridge_relay.rs intercepts FspecCommandResult (does NOT forward as regular chunk), formats as commandResponse OutboundMessage with matching request_id
7. Relay endpoint translates OutboundMessage to relay protocol format and sends to relay

KEY TYPES:
- FspecCommandRequest (StreamChunk type in codelet/napi/src/types.rs) — emitted by bridge_relay.rs when command arrives, AND by session_manager.rs when LLM invokes Fspec tool
- FspecCommandResult (StreamChunk type) — result flowing back, intercepted by bridge_relay.rs for commandResponse
- InboundMessage (bridge_relay.rs) — extended with 'command' type, request_id, command, args_json fields
- OutboundMessage (bridge.rs) — extended with optional request_id for commandResponse messages
- fspecCallback (src/utils/fspec-callback.ts) — the shared in-process command executor, called ONLY by GlobalSessionStreamManager

Uses 'ws' npm package for both client and server.

BRIDGE-015.description: Create a new bridge endpoint (alongside the existing Telegram endpoint) that connects fspec to the platform-agnostic relay server. Unlike the Telegram endpoint which translates to Telegram Bot API, this endpoint speaks the relay protocol directly — handling the 5 session-scoped message types (input, sessionControl, command, commandResponse, chunk) plus auth handshake. The key new capability vs Telegram: handling 'command' messages by forwarding them through bridge_relay.rs into the FspecCommandRequest/FspecCommandResult StreamChunk event system, where GlobalSessionStreamManager calls fspecCallback — the same path used when the LLM invokes the Fspec tool. The relay endpoint is a PURE PROTOCOL TRANSLATOR and does NOT call fspecCallback directly. This is the fspec-side counterpart to MOBILE-010 in the fspec-mobile project.

examples.text: Endpoint starts, connects to relay ws://relay.example.com, sends auth with channel_id and api_key, receives authSuccess with instances list
Endpoint sends auth with invalid api_key, receives authError with code INVALID_API_KEY, logs error and exits
codelet BridgeTool connects to endpoint WS server, sends connected message, endpoint learns session_id for routing

Relay sends {type:input, session_id:X, data:{message:'fix bug', images:[...]}} → endpoint translates to flat InboundMessage {type:input, session_id:X, message:'fix bug', images:[...]} → forwards to codelet WS
Relay sends {type:sessionControl, session_id:X, data:{action:interrupt}} → endpoint translates to {type:control, session_id:X, action:interrupt} → forwards to codelet WS
codelet sends chunk StreamChunk → endpoint forwards to relay as {type:chunk, session_id:X, data:StreamChunk} with no transformation
Endpoint starts without RELAY_URL env var → exits with clear error message explaining required configuration
Relay connection drops → endpoint logs warning, attempts reconnection with exponential backoff, re-authenticates on reconnect

Relay sends {type:input, session_id:'unknown-session', data:{message:'hello'}} but no codelet is connected with that session_id → endpoint logs warning 'No codelet connection for session unknown-session' and drops the message

Two codelet BridgeTools connect simultaneously with different session_ids (session-A, session-B). Relay sends input for session-A → endpoint routes to session-A's WS connection only. Relay sends input for session-B → endpoint routes to session-B's WS connection only.

Relay sends {type:command, session_id:X, request_id:R1, data:{command:'board', args:{}}} → endpoint translates to InboundMessage {type:'command', session_id:X, request_id:R1, command:'board', args_json:'{}'} → forwards to codelet WS → bridge_relay.rs emits FspecCommandRequest StreamChunk → GlobalSessionStreamManager calls fspecCallback → FspecCommandResult flows back through broadcast channel → bridge_relay.rs sends {type:'commandResponse', session_id:X, request_id:R1, data:{command:'board', success:true, result:{...}}}

Relay sends command that takes 45 seconds → bridge_relay.rs emits FspecCommandRequest → fspecCallback execution exceeds pipeline timeout (same timeout as LLM-invoked Fspec tool) → FspecCommandResult with error flows back through broadcast channel → bridge_relay.rs sends commandResponse with success:false and timeout error preserving request_id

Relay sends command for unknown fspec command → command flows through bridge_relay.rs → FspecCommandRequest → fspecCallback returns error → FspecCommandResult with success:false flows back → bridge_relay.rs sends commandResponse with error message and preserved request_id

rules.text: Endpoint is a standalone WebSocket server in bridge/ directory (like telegram-endpoint.ts), started independently
Endpoint connects to the relay server as a WebSocket CLIENT (relay is the server), unlike Telegram where fspec connects TO the endpoint
Auth handshake: endpoint sends {type:auth, data:{channel_id, api_key}} on connect and waits for authSuccess/authError before processing messages
chunk and connected messages pass through from fspec to relay with no transformation needed
sessionControl from relay must be renamed to 'control' and data unwrapped when forwarding to fspec bridge

Relay protocol uses camelCase message types (sessionControl, commandResponse) matching the mobile app implementation, and wraps payloads in {data:{...}} envelope. fspec InboundMessage uses flat fields (message, action) and 'control' instead of 'sessionControl'. Endpoint translates between these formats in both directions. NOTE: Part 3 architecture notes use snake_case (session_control, command_response) but the actual implementations use camelCase.

Endpoint supports multiple concurrent codelet sessions. Each codelet BridgeTool connects to the local WS server and identifies itself with a session_id via the connected message. Endpoint maintains a session_id→WebSocket map for routing inbound relay messages to the correct codelet connection.
Endpoint initiates periodic ping messages to the relay server to keep the connection alive (same pattern as mobile app). Relay responds with pong. Ping interval is 30 seconds.

Configuration via env vars: RELAY_URL (full WebSocket URL including path, e.g. ws://relay.example.com/v1/ws), RELAY_CHANNEL_ID, RELAY_API_KEY, WEBSOCKET_PORT (local port for codelet BridgeTool connections, default 8080)

StreamChunk data from fspec is forwarded to the relay without internal field transformation. fspec uses {type: 'tool_call'} (snake_case), mobile currently expects {chunkType: 'toolCall'} (camelCase). MOBILE-010 is responsible for updating the mobile app to handle fspec's native StreamChunk format — the relay endpoint does NOT translate chunk internals.

Messages from relay targeting an unknown or disconnected session_id are logged as warnings and silently dropped. No error response is sent back to the relay for session-scoped messages (input, sessionControl).

Must handle all 5 message types: input (session→fspec), sessionControl (session→fspec), command (session→fspec), commandResponse (fspec→client), chunk (fspec→client). ALL message types are session-scoped. Commands provide a separate channel within the session for fspec CLI operations, distinct from the agent conversation (input/chunk).

command messages are session-scoped and use request/response pattern with request_id correlation. Commands flow through the session's bridge WebSocket to Rust bridge_relay.rs, which channels them through the FspecCommandRequest/FspecCommandResult StreamChunk event system via fspecCallback. The relay endpoint does NOT call fspecCallback directly — it is a pure protocol translator.

InboundMessage in bridge_relay.rs must be extended to support 'command' type with request_id, command name, and args_json fields. When bridge_relay.rs receives a command InboundMessage, it emits a FspecCommandRequest StreamChunk into the session. GlobalSessionStreamManager handles it by calling fspecCallback. The FspecCommandResult StreamChunk flows back through the session's broadcast channel. bridge_relay.rs intercepts FspecCommandResult chunks (does NOT forward them as regular chunks) and sends a commandResponse OutboundMessage with the matching request_id back through the bridge WebSocket.

commandResponse uses canonical format: {type:'commandResponse', request_id, session_id, data:{command, success, result, error}} where success and error are derived from fspec's FspecCommandResult. OutboundMessage must be extended to support request_id for commandResponse messages.

Command execution timeout is handled within the FspecCommandRequest/FspecCommandResult pipeline — the same mechanism and timeout that applies when the LLM invokes the Fspec tool. The relay endpoint does not implement its own timeout via Promise.race.

BUG-047.description:
# Bug Report: BUG-047

## Type Mismatches in record-metric and record-tokens Commands

**Discovered during**: LOCK-002 file locking refactoring
**Date**: 2025-10-28
**Reporter**: Claude (AI Assistant)

---

## Summary

Two command files have type mismatches between their function signatures and how they're called in command registration:
- `src/commands/record-metric.ts`
- `src/commands/record-tokens.ts`

These bugs existed **before** the LOCK-002 refactoring work began.

---

## Detailed Findings

### File 1: `src/commands/record-metric.ts`

**Function Signature** (lines 19-23):
```typescript
export async function recordMetric(options: {
  workUnitId: string;
  tokens: number;
  cwd?: string;
}): Promise<{ success: boolean; totalTokens?: number }>
```

**Command Registration Call** (lines 66-70):
```typescript
await recordMetric({
  metric,                    // ❌ Not in function signature
  value: parseFloat(value),  // ❌ Not in function signature
  unit: options.unit,        // ❌ Not in function signature
});
```

**Command Arguments** (lines 60-62):
```typescript
.argument('<metric>', 'Metric name')
.argument('<value>', 'Metric value')
.option('--unit <unit>', 'Unit of measurement')
```

**Problem**: The function expects `{ workUnitId, tokens, cwd }` but is called with `{ metric, value, unit }`. These are completely different parameter sets.

---

### File 2: `src/commands/record-tokens.ts`

**Function Signature** (lines 19-23):
```typescript
export async function recordTokens(options: {
  workUnitId: string;
  tokens: number;
  cwd?: string;
}): Promise<{ success: boolean; totalTokens?: number }>
```

**Command Registration Call** (lines 76-79):
```typescript
await recordTokens({
  workUnitId,
  tokens: parseInt(tokens, 10),
  operation: options.operation,  // ❌ Not in function signature
});
```

**Command Option** (lines 65-68):
```typescript
.option(
  '--operation <operation>',
  'Operation type (e.g., specification, implementation)'
)
```

**Problem**: The function doesn't accept an `operation` parameter but the command tries to pass it anyway.

---

## Impact Analysis

### Current State
- TypeScript compilation may be passing due to the `[key: string]: unknown` index signature in the options interface
- Commands may be silently failing or ignoring parameters
- Tests may not be covering these code paths

### Expected Behavior
The function signatures should match the command registration calls exactly.

### Potential Fixes

#### Option A: Update Function Signatures (Recommended)
Match the functions to what the commands actually need:

**record-metric.ts:**
```typescript
export async function recordMetric(options: {
  metric: string;
  value: number;
  unit?: string;
  cwd?: string;
}): Promise<{ success: boolean }>
```

**record-tokens.ts:**
```typescript
export async function recordTokens(options: {
  workUnitId: string;
  tokens: number;
  operation?: string;
  cwd?: string;
}): Promise<{ success: boolean; totalTokens?: number }>
```

#### Option B: Update Command Registration
Change how commands call the functions to match existing signatures (may require rethinking command purpose).

---

## Discovery Context

These bugs were discovered during LOCK-002 refactoring when:
1. Systematically refactoring command files to use `fileManager.transaction()`
2. Applied standard pattern to these files
3. Ran full test suite: **103 tests failed**
4. Investigated failures and found pre-existing type mismatches
5. Reverted changes to these files to isolate the issue

**Git References:**
- Last good commit before discovery: `efee27c`
- Files were at HEAD~1 when bug discovered

---

## Reproduction Steps

1. Review `src/commands/record-metric.ts` lines 19-23 and 66-70
2. Review `src/commands/record-tokens.ts` lines 19-23 and 76-79
3. Note the parameter mismatch between function signatures and calls
4. Run: `npm run build` - TypeScript may pass due to index signature
5. Run: `npm test` - Tests may fail or pass if not covering these paths

---

## Recommended Actions

1. **Investigate Intent**: Determine what these commands are supposed to do
   - Are they for recording metrics OR token usage?
   - Should they operate on work units?

2. **Fix Type Signatures**: Align function signatures with command usage

3. **Add Tests**: Ensure test coverage for these commands

4. **Update Documentation**: Clarify command purpose and usage

5. **Continue LOCK-002**: These files can be refactored after types are fixed

---

## Notes

- These bugs existed **before LOCK-002 refactoring**
- Type system may not catch due to index signature: `[key: string]: unknown`
- May need to check if similar patterns exist in other command files
- Should verify if commands are actually used in production

---

## Related Work Units

- **LOCK-002**: File locking refactoring (blocked by this bug for these 2 files)

architectureNotes.text: Current implementation in src/utils/step-validation.ts uses hardcoded regex: /^\/\/\s*@step\s+(Given|When|Then|And|But)\s+(.+)$/ on line 53-54

BUG-063.description: The @step validation in src/utils/step-validation.ts is hardcoded to match only JavaScript-style // comments. It should be language-agnostic and match @step annotations regardless of the comment syntax used (e.g., //, #, --, %, ', /* */, etc.). Currently it uses regex patterns like /^\/\/\s*@step\s+(Given|When|Then|And|But)\s+(.+)$/ which only match // comments.

examples.text: JavaScript: // @step Given a dog shits in the woods → should extract 'Given a dog shits in the woods'
Python: # @step When I click the button → should extract 'When I click the button'
SQL: -- @step Then I see the result → should extract 'Then I see the result'
Block comment: /* @step Given a dog shits in the woods */ → should extract 'Given a dog shits in the woods'
MATLAB: % @step And the database is updated → should extract 'And the database is updated'
Visual Basic: ' @step But the error is logged → should extract 'But the error is logged'

rules.text: @step validation must be language-agnostic and support all comment syntaxes
Must match @step anywhere in a comment line, not just at the start after //
Must extract only the step text between keyword and end of step, ignoring comment delimiters
Must support block comments like /* @step Given text */ and line comments like // @step, # @step, -- @step, % @step, ' @step

BUG-063.title: @step validation hardcoded to JavaScript comment syntax, should be language-agnostic

BUG-079.description:
The prefill detection regex matches ANY text inside square brackets, causing false positives when Gherkin steps describe code syntax like 'workUnitsData.workUnits[id]'.

Root cause: Overly broad regex pattern matches [anything] instead of specific placeholder patterns we generate.

Impact: 
- Valid feature files blocked from workflow progression
- Forces workarounds (rewording steps to avoid brackets)
- Breaks when describing array access, generics, or other bracket syntax

Fix: Only detect actual placeholder patterns we generate:
- [role], [action], [benefit] (user story placeholders)
- [precondition], [expected outcome] (step placeholders)  
- TODO: markers (architecture note placeholders)
- @component, @critical (tag placeholders)

Do NOT match arbitrary bracket syntax that happens to be in step descriptions.

Step 'When I access array[index] in code' should NOT be flagged as placeholder

rules.text: Prefill detection MUST only match actual placeholder text patterns we generate: [role], [action], [benefit], [precondition], [expected outcome], TODO:
Prefill detection MUST NOT match arbitrary bracket syntax like array access [id], TypeScript generics Array<T>, or code examples

architectureNotes.text: Implementation uses the `diffy` crate for three-way merge (diffy::merge). Add `diffy = "1"` to codelet/git/Cargo.toml. The `similar` crate already present only supports two-way diff — not three-way merge with conflict markers.

New function `write_conflict_markers()` in session_result.rs: takes base/session/main content for each conflicting file, runs diffy::merge(), writes result to worktree file. Called BEFORE returning ConflictError in apply_session_changes().

detect_conflicts() currently compares raw bytes. For the three-way merge, we need to also consider: (1) identical changes = not a real conflict, (2) non-overlapping changes in same file = auto-merge, no conflict. diffy handles this automatically when its merge result has no conflicts.

The TypeScript layer (conflictLlmContext.ts, mergeWorktreeHandler.ts) needs NO changes. The fix is entirely in the Rust layer — write markers into worktree files so that the existing 'read file + resolve markers' instruction to the LLM actually works.

BUG-098.description:
When /merge-worktree detects conflicts, the Rust code in apply_session_changes() (session_result.rs) returns Err(GitError::ConflictError) immediately without writing conflict markers into the worktree files. The TypeScript handler then tells the LLM to 'read each conflicting file, resolve the git conflict markers (<<<<<<< / ======= / >>>>>>>)' — but the markers don't exist in the files. The LLM reads the file, finds no markers, gets confused, and enters a loop.

The root cause is that detect_conflicts() does a pure divergence check (did both session and main change the same file since base?) and returns file names only. No three-way merge is performed, so no conflict markers are ever materialized in the worktree.

Reproduced in session 9f4fec89 on 2026-02-26: user edited README.md ('The' → 'Da'), main had also diverged on README.md, /merge-worktree fired the conflict path, LLM read the worktree file — no markers found.

examples.text: Session edits line 7 of README.md ('The' → 'Da'), main also changed line 7 ('The Spec-Driven' → 'The Spec-Driven (v2.0)') → worktree README.md gets <<<<<<< session / Da Spec-Driven / ======= / The Spec-Driven (v2.0) / >>>>>>> main
Session edits src/app.ts (lines 10-15), main edits src/app.ts (lines 40-50, no overlap) → three-way merge succeeds cleanly, no conflict markers needed, file NOT in conflict list
Session adds new file utils.ts, main also adds utils.ts with different content → conflict markers written with empty base (two-way diff)
Session modifies logo.png (binary), main also modifies logo.png → binary file listed as conflicting but NO conflict markers written (binary can't be merged), error message notes binary conflicts
Session and main both change line 7 of README.md identically ('The' → 'Da') → detect_conflicts() should NOT report this as a conflict (both made same change)
After conflict markers are written, LLM reads the file, sees <<<<<<< markers, resolves them, saves, runs /merge-worktree again → second merge succeeds

rules.text: When apply_session_changes() detects conflicting files, it must perform a three-way merge and write standard git conflict markers into the worktree files BEFORE returning ConflictError
Conflict markers must follow standard git format: <<<<<<< session (your changes) / ======= / >>>>>>> main
Binary files must be skipped during three-way merge — no conflict markers written for binary content
For files added in both session and main with different content, write conflict markers with empty base (two-way conflict)
The worktree files must be overwritten with the merged content containing conflict markers — the LLM reads from the worktree path
Files where both session and main made identical changes (no actual conflict) should NOT get conflict markers
The ConflictError must still be returned after writing markers — the error signals the TypeScript handler to show conflict guidance

BUG-098.title: Merge conflict markers never written to worktree files — LLM told to resolve markers that don't exist

userStory.action: merge worktree changes when conflicts exist
userStory.benefit: see actual conflict markers in the files so I can resolve them

architectureNotes.text: The root cause is that fspec has no equivalent of `git add` to mark a conflict as resolved. Real git uses the index (staging area) — once you `git add` a conflicted file, git stops flagging it. fspec's merge system is stateless: every /merge-worktree call re-detects conflicts from scratch by comparing worktree vs base vs main. The fix adds statefulness via .fspec-pending-conflicts.

Implementation: New function check_pending_conflicts(worktree_path) in session_result.rs. Reads .fspec-pending-conflicts (JSON array of file paths). For each file, checks if worktree file content contains '<<<<<<< '. Returns (resolved: Vec<String>, still_pending: Vec<String>). Called at the TOP of apply_session_changes(), BEFORE detect_conflicts().

Flow change in apply_session_changes(): (1) Check .fspec-pending-conflicts → if exists, partition into resolved/pending. (2) If any still_pending → return ConflictError with just those files (no marker regeneration). (3) If all resolved → delete state file, exclude resolved files from detect_conflicts (they've been user-accepted), merge remaining changes normally, copy resolved worktree content directly to main.

The BUG-098 test 'test_re_merge_after_resolution_succeeds' (three_way_merge.rs:474) tests three_way_merge_text() directly with session_resolved == main — this tests the MERGE function in isolation, but the actual bug is one layer UP in apply_session_changes() where detect_conflicts() fires BEFORE the merge function is even called. New integration tests must test the full apply_session_changes() flow.

tree_utils.rs collect_worktree_files() must skip .fspec-pending-conflicts (add to is_git_or_fspec_dir or add a filename-based filter). Also add it to .gitignore pattern if using the excludes stack approach.

BUG-099.description:
After BUG-098 fixed conflict marker writing, a second bug remains: when the LLM resolves conflict markers and runs /merge-worktree again, detect_conflicts() re-reads the worktree files (now containing the resolved content), compares session-resolved vs base and main vs base, and sees both sides still differ from base — so it declares a NEW conflict. write_conflict_markers() then overwrites the LLM's resolution with fresh conflict markers. The LLM resolves again, merges again, same thing happens — infinite loop until the user kills the session.

Root cause: detect_conflicts() compares worktree (session) content against the base commit, not against main. After the LLM resolves markers, the worktree content is the resolved version which differs from base. Main also differs from base. So both sides are 'changed' → conflict detected again. The three-way merge regenerates markers because it uses the original base, the resolved worktree (as 'session'), and main — producing new conflict markers.

Reproduced in debug session bb90f15f (2026-02-26T23:51:12): README.md conflict detected 3 times in 76 seconds before user killed session. Sequences 3→25 (first conflict+resolve), 43→64 (second conflict+resolve), 80→82 (third conflict started, user exits).

examples.text: When LLM resolves worktree README.md to match main exactly (content equal), then /merge-worktree re-runs → detect_conflicts() sees worktree==main → NOT a conflict → apply_session_changes copies resolved content → merge succeeds → session cleaned up

When LLM resolves worktree README.md to a THIRD value (neither session nor main original), then /merge-worktree re-runs → detect_conflicts() sees worktree≠main AND worktree≠base → still a conflict → three-way merge runs with resolved-content as 'session' → if resolved doesn't overlap with main's changes, auto-merges cleanly; if it overlaps, new conflict markers appear (this is correct behavior — user made a bad resolution)

Exact reproduction from debug session bb90f15f: base='The', session→'Ma', main→'Those'. First merge writes markers. LLM resolves by keeping 'Ma' (session's choice). Second merge: worktree='Ma' ≠ base ✓, main='Those' ≠ base ✓ → CONFLICT AGAIN. three_way_merge(base='The', session='Ma', main='Those') → overlapping change → NEW markers written, overwriting LLM's work. Same resolution. Same conflict. Loop 3x in 76s before user kills session.

First merge of README.md: no .fspec-pending-conflicts exists → detect_conflicts finds divergence → write_conflict_markers writes markers AND creates .fspec-pending-conflicts with ['README.md'] → ConflictError returned

Re-merge after LLM resolves README.md (removes markers, keeps 'Ma'): .fspec-pending-conflicts exists listing README.md → check worktree: no <<<<<<< found → README.md is RESOLVED → skip three-way merge → use worktree content as final → apply to main → merge succeeds → NO LOOP

Re-merge with markers still in file: .fspec-pending-conflicts lists README.md → check worktree: <<<<<<< found → NOT resolved yet → return ConflictError listing README.md → LLM told 'still has markers' → no overwrite, no re-generation of markers

Multi-file conflict with partial resolution: .fspec-pending-conflicts lists [README.md, config.yml]. LLM resolves README.md (markers removed) but not config.yml (markers remain). Re-merge: README.md → resolved, config.yml → still pending → ConflictError lists only config.yml

Re-merge with unresolved markers produces DOUBLE-NESTED corruption: worktree has '<<<<<<< session
<<<<<<< session
session-v
=======
main-v
>>>>>>> main
=======
main-v
>>>>>>> main' — because detect_conflicts feeds marker-containing content as 'session' to three_way_merge, which then wraps the markers in NEW markers. This makes the file unresolvable.

rules.text: When the LLM resolves conflict markers and /merge-worktree is called again, apply_session_changes() must compare the worktree content against main content — if they match, skip that file (conflict resolved)
The fix must be in the Rust layer only (detect_conflicts in session_result.rs) — no TypeScript changes needed
The existing three-way merge logic in three_way_merge.rs must NOT be modified — the bug is in the caller (detect_conflicts), not the merge algorithm

The BUG-098 test 'test_re_merge_after_resolution_succeeds' is flawed — it passes session_resolved (matching main) which makes the three-way merge return Clean, but the REAL re-merge path goes through detect_conflicts() FIRST which still flags it as a conflict before the merge even runs

On re-merge (when .fspec-pending-conflicts exists), for each previously-conflicted file: if the worktree file no longer contains <<<<<<< markers → treat as resolved, use worktree content as final answer, skip three-way merge for that file

On re-merge, if a previously-conflicted file still contains <<<<<<< markers → user hasn't finished resolving → report as still conflicting (do NOT re-generate markers, just re-return ConflictError for that file)

Once all previously-conflicted files are resolved (none contain markers), delete .fspec-pending-conflicts and proceed with apply — the resolved worktree content is copied to main as the user's final answer
.fspec-pending-conflicts must be excluded from collect_worktree_files() so it doesn't get applied to main as a regular file

When write_conflict_markers() returns actual conflicts, apply_session_changes() must persist a .fspec-pending-conflicts state file (JSON with 'files' array) in the worktree listing those files — this distinguishes 'first conflict detection' from 're-merge after resolution'

On re-merge with unresolved markers, the current code produces DOUBLE-NESTED markers (markers inside markers) because detect_conflicts() feeds the marker-containing content as 'session' to three_way_merge — this corrupts the file and makes manual resolution impossible. The fix MUST prevent re-running three-way merge on files that already contain conflict markers

BUG-099.title: Re-merge after conflict resolution enters infinite loop — detect_conflicts() re-detects resolved files as conflicting

userStory.action: resolve merge conflict markers and re-run /merge-worktree
userStory.benefit: my resolved file is accepted and the merge completes without looping

architectureNotes.text: The apply_patch tool is implemented as a standalone rig::tool::Tool struct (not through facade traits) since it has no equivalent in other providers. It takes a single 'patch' string parameter, parses the Codex freeform format, then delegates to internal file operations (create, edit, delete). It lives in codelet/tools/src/apply_patch.rs.

BUG-105.description: In Codex-backed sessions, the assistant appears to lack a first-class `apply_patch` tool call and instead falls back to wrapping `apply_patch` inside a shell command. This is incorrect behavior for file editing workflows and leads to failed shell invocations like `sh: apply_patch: command not found`, even though patch/edit operations should be available as proper tool calls. The issue aligns with openai/codex#2005 and should be fixed in the Codex tool-calling facade so patch/edit capabilities are exposed and selected correctly instead of degrading to shell execution.

Agent calls apply_patch with multiple file operations in one patch → all operations are applied atomically
Agent sends malformed patch text missing '*** Begin Patch' → apply_patch returns a clear error
Agent calls apply_patch with Update File but context lines don't match → apply_patch returns an error describing the mismatch

BUG-106.description: DeepSearch fails for ZAI/GLM provider with HTTP 500 error. Investigation shows the main session loop (which uses streaming) works fine for ZAI, but DeepSearch uses the non-streaming prompt() path. The ONLY HTTP-level difference is that streaming adds {"stream": true} to the request. Z.AI's non-streaming code path likely has a server-side issue with tool-calling requests. Additionally, rig's OpenAI CompletionRequest::try_from silently drops max_tokens (the .. rest pattern discards it), so max_tokens should be included in additional_params to actually reach the Z.AI API.

ZAI DeepSearch config includes max_tokens: 8192 in additional_params alongside temperature and top_p
Non-ZAI/non-Codex providers (claude, openai, gemini) remain non-streaming for DeepSearch

max_tokens must be included in ZAI additional_params since rig's OpenAI CompletionRequest silently drops it from CoreCompletionRequest

BUG-111.description:
The CodexGrepFilesFacade in codelet/tools/src/facade/codex.rs exposes `include` and `limit` in its schema but map_params() only consumes `pattern` and `path`. The `include` glob filter and `limit` for max results are silently ignored.

This is especially critical because `grep_files` with `include` is the Codex-native way to do glob-like file matching — Codex has NO standalone `glob` tool (removed in BUG-107). Without `include` working, the model has NO way to filter searches by file type.

The fix requires: (1) extending InternalSearchParams::Grep with include/limit fields, (2) updating map_params to extract them, (3) wiring them through SearchToolFacadeWrapper to GrepTool, (4) updating GrepArgs, and (5) updating all other facades that construct InternalSearchParams::Grep.

The underlying GrepTool already supports glob filtering via a 'glob' param (grep.rs line 221-256) — it's just never reached because the facade drops the include param before it gets there.

Model sends {"pattern": ".", "include": "*.rs", "limit": 10} → only 10 file paths returned even if hundreds match
Model sends {"pattern": "TODO"} with no include/limit → all files searched, all results returned (backward compatible)
ZAI and Gemini grep facades continue to work with include=None and limit=None (non-breaking change)

InternalSearchParams::Grep must include optional 'include' and 'limit' fields so facades can pass them through
SearchToolFacadeWrapper must pass 'include' as 'glob' to GrepTool.execute() args (because GrepTool already supports glob filtering via the 'glob' key)

BUG-114.description:
The Codex CLI model is trained on `shell` (raw execvp with argv array) and `exec_command` (PTY-capable unified exec with yield_time_ms). These are missing from the Codex facade.

With the new unified exec tool (TOOL-016), create Codex-specific facade wrappers that map these Codex-native tool names and schemas to the provider-agnostic unified exec tool:

1. `shell` facade → maps command (Array<String>), workdir, timeout_ms to unified exec run action with shell interpretation disabled
2. `exec_command` facade → maps cmd, workdir, shell, tty, yield_time_ms, max_output_tokens, login to unified exec run action with full PTY support

Both facades follow the existing CodexShellCommandFacade pattern in codelet/tools/src/facade/codex.rs, using FacadeToolWrapper for Codex-native parameter schemas while delegating to the shared unified exec implementation.

The exec_command facade must return session_id in its output when the process is still running, so the model can follow up with write_stdin (BUG-115).

BUG-117.description:
TOOL-017 and BUG-116 implemented the request_user_input HITL tool and Codex facade, but the session manager's HITL handler was wired using the wrong pattern (StreamChunk intercept via GlobalSessionStreamManager). The correct pattern is the PAUSE pattern — the HITL handler stores questions in session state, sets status to Paused, blocks on mpsc, and TypeScript polls the state via NAPI getter and renders inline UI in InputTransition.

The fix:
1. HITL handler closure sets hitl_request state + set_status(Paused) + blocks (like pause handler)
2. NAPI getter session_get_hitl_request returns questions when paused
3. useRustSessionState adds hitlRequest to snapshot
4. InputTransition renders inline multi-step question UI (↑/↓ options, Enter advance, Esc cancel)
5. AgentView keyboard handler captures input and calls sessionSendHitlResponse
6. Remove wrong-pattern code: HitlRequest StreamChunk, GlobalSessionStreamManager intercept, setHitlHandler/clearHitlHandler

examples.text: LLM calls request_user_input with 2 questions → handler stores questions in hitl_request state → sets status to Paused → React re-renders → InputTransition shows first question with options → user presses ↑/↓ and Enter → advances to second question → user selects and presses Enter → sessionSendHitlResponse called with all answers → handler unblocks and returns
LLM calls request_user_input → InputTransition shows question inline → user presses Escape → sessionSendHitlResponse called with cancelled=true → handler unblocks → facade converts to ToolError
Session is paused with hitl_request → useRustSessionState polls sessionGetHitlRequest → snapshot.hitlRequest has questions array → InputTransition renders inline question UI
Session ends → cleanup calls set_hitl_handler(session_id, None) and clears hitl_request state → if handler was blocked, recv returns Cancelled fallback
No HITL handler registered (headless mode) → execute_hitl returns error immediately → tool returns unavailable message — no pause, no blocking
Question with options renders: ⏸ icon, question header, question text, ● selected option / ○ unselected options, navigation hints — same visual location as pause UI
Question without options (freeform only) renders: question text + text input area — user types and presses Enter to submit answer

The HITL handler closure MUST follow the pause pattern: store hitl_request state on BackgroundSession, set_status(Paused), wait_for_hitl_response (block), then clear state and set_status(Running) on response
BackgroundSession MUST have hitl_request: RwLock<Option<HitlRequestState>> storing the questions while waiting for user response, alongside existing hitl_response_tx/rx channel pair
A session_get_hitl_request NAPI function MUST exist for TypeScript to poll the current HITL questions when session is paused — following the same pattern as session_get_pause_state
useRustSessionState MUST add hitlRequest field to RustSessionSnapshot, fetched via getHitlRequest(sessionId) in rustStateSource when isPaused is true
InputTransition MUST render HITL questions inline when isPaused and hitlRequest is present — showing current question with selectable options and freeform input, same rendering location as pause UI
AgentView MUST have a useInputCompat handler for HITL that captures ↑/↓ to navigate options, Enter to select/advance, Esc to cancel — and calls sessionSendHitlResponse with the collected answers
Pressing Escape during HITL MUST call sessionSendHitlResponse with cancelled=true to unblock the Rust handler
The HitlRequest StreamChunk variant, GlobalSessionStreamManager intercept, setHitlHandler/clearHitlHandler, and handleHitlRequest MUST be removed — these were the wrong pattern

BUG-119.description: Regression from TUI-079 (commit a764bd46). Switching globalStreamListener from updateWorkUnitsFromWatcher() to loadData() fixed data correctness but introduced severe flickering. Root causes: (1) loadData() acquires filesystem locks that collide with concurrent CLI/agent writes, producing 'Lock file is already being held' errors that flash the ErrorView, (2) zero JavaScript-side debouncing means multiple concurrent loadData() calls from watcher + IPC + explicit calls after move operations, (3) loadData() unconditionally clears error state before reading, causing board→error→board oscillation, (4) redundant explicit loadData() after moveWorkUnitUp/Down doubles lock contention with the watcher-triggered one.

examples.text: AI agent writes to work-units.json (holding write lock) while watcher fires loadData() → loadData() gets ELOCKED error → board remains stable, no error screen flash, watcher retries after debounce succeeds
User presses ] to move work unit down → work unit moves in the board, watcher fires once (debounced), no double-load or lock contention
Multiple rapid external changes to work-units.json within 200ms → single loadData() call executes after debounce, board updates once smoothly
loadData() is already running when watcher triggers another → second call is silently skipped, no lock contention
Real errors like permission denied or disk full still show the ErrorView — only lock contention is silenced

rules.text: Lock contention errors (ELOCKED / 'Lock file is already being held') must be treated as transient and must NOT set the error state or trigger an ErrorView render
globalStreamListener must debounce loadData() calls on the JavaScript side (on top of the Rust 100ms debounce) so that rapid watcher events coalesce into a single load
Concurrent loadData() calls must be prevented — if a loadData() is already in-flight, subsequent calls must be skipped (not queued)
loadData() must NOT clear the error state before attempting to read — error clearing must only happen on successful read
Explicit loadData() calls after moveWorkUnitUp/Down in BoardView must be removed — the file watcher already triggers a debounced loadData() after the write
All existing TUI-079 correctness behavior must be preserved — loadData() path, session context sync, deleted work unit detection, ordering from states arrays

BUG-120.description: The /role command and set_role AgentManager action store a role string in BackgroundSession.role (RwLock<Option<String>>) but the role is never injected into the LLM conversation. The run_with_provider! macro in session_manager.rs always passes None as the preamble to create_rig_agent(), and no SystemReminderType::Role exists. The role is pure metadata — queryable via AgentManager list/get_status and used as sender attribution in inter-session messages — but has zero effect on the LLM's behavior. The fix is to add a SystemReminderType::Role variant and inject the role text as a system reminder whenever set_role is called.

examples.text: User sets role 'You are a security reviewer' via /role dialog → system reminder injected → LLM on next turn receives the role text and adopts the security reviewer persona
Agent calls set_role with role='code-reviewer' on a subordinate session → subordinate's messages get a role system reminder → subordinate behaves as a code reviewer
User changes role from 'architect' to 'tester' via /role → new system reminder supersedes old one → LLM adopts tester persona on next turn
User clears role via /role (empty text) → role system reminder is removed from messages → LLM reverts to default behavior
Supervisor spawns a subordinate with role='test-writer' → subordinate session has role reminder before receiving its first message

rules.text: When a role is set on a session, it must be injected into the LLM conversation as a system reminder so the AI adopts that role
When spawn is called with a role parameter, the role system reminder is injected into the new session before it receives its first message
The run_with_provider! macro reads session.get_role() and passes it as the preamble parameter to create_rig_agent

Each provider incorporates the role preamble into its system prompt using its own facade/builder — Claude via SystemPromptFacade, Gemini via build_gemini_system_prompt, OpenAI/ZAI via prepend_fspec_guidance, Codex by appending to CODEX_BASE_INSTRUCTIONS
When a role is cleared (empty string), the preamble reverts to None and each provider falls back to its default system prompt (no custom role text)
The role is read fresh each turn — a role change via set_role takes effect on the very next turn without restart
Codex provider always preserves CODEX_BASE_INSTRUCTIONS — role text is appended, never replaces the base instructions

CMPCT-002.description:
When compaction is triggered during Gemini continuation (empty tool_use), the current code errors out. This should be handled gracefully by breaking out of the continuation loop and returning a signal to trigger compaction, then retrying the turn.

## Current Behavior
- Logs error: 'Compaction triggered during Gemini continuation - not yet supported'
- Returns Err() which fails the session
- User loses work in progress

## Desired Behavior  
- Break out of continuation loop gracefully
- Save any partial progress (continuation_text)
- Return a signal indicating compaction is needed
- Calling code triggers compaction and retries the turn

## Implementation
1. Add StreamLoopResult::NeedsCompaction variant
2. Change error case to return this signal
3. Handle signal in calling code to trigger compaction

## Research
See attached research document analyzing how OpenCode and VTCode handle this.

examples.text: Given Gemini model is in continuation (empty tool_use received), When compaction threshold is exceeded (PromptCancelled error), Then system saves partial continuation_text, updates token tracker, returns NeedsCompaction

Given session has accumulated 180K tokens (90% of 200K context window), When Gemini continuation triggers next request, And request is cancelled due to token limit, Then session does NOT fail, And user sees 'Compacting context...' message, And session continues after compaction
Given Gemini model has produced partial response text during continuation, When compaction is triggered, Then partial text is preserved in session history, And user does not lose any model output

rules.text: When compaction is triggered during Gemini continuation, the system MUST break out of the continuation loop gracefully instead of erroring
Any partial text accumulated during continuation MUST be saved to the session before signaling compaction
Token tracker MUST be updated with cumulative billing before signaling compaction
The stream loop MUST return a distinct NeedsCompaction result variant so callers can trigger compaction and retry

CMPCT-003.description: When auto-compaction triggers (post-loop or pre-prompt), the TUI's "Thinking..." indicator disappears instead of transitioning to "Compacting...". Root cause: CompactionComplete event fires after the in-memory setup phase (~5ms) but BEFORE the actual DAG construction work. The entire DAG construction phase (SessionSearch + inject_summary calls) runs with session status=Idle, so the UI shows no activity. Two fixes needed: (1) Don't emit CompactionComplete until after inject_summary applies the DAG, (2) CompactionContinuing should set status to Running or keep Compacting throughout. See attached investigation for full code trace.

examples.text: Post-loop compaction: agent finishes (Done→Idle), compaction triggers (CompactionStarted→Compacting), execute_compaction runs (~5ms), CompactionContinuing→Running, retry stream runs (status stays Running), stream finishes (Done→Idle), apply_pending_dag, emit CompactionComplete

Pre-prompt compaction: threshold exceeded before API call → CompactionStarted→Compacting, execute_compaction (~5ms), CompactionContinuing→Running, main stream processes compaction instruction, Done→Idle, apply_pending_dag, emit CompactionComplete
No DAG pending: agent responds normally without compaction. Done→Idle. No CompactionComplete emitted from agent_loop (apply_pending_dag returns false)

rules.text: CompactionComplete must NOT be emitted from stream_loop after execute_compaction() returns — the setup phase is not the completion
CompactionComplete must only be emitted from agent_loop after apply_pending_dag() succeeds
CompactionContinuing in NAPI BackgroundOutput::emit must set status to Running (not be a no-op) so the UI shows activity during DAG construction
Session status must never be Idle while the agent is actively processing (streaming, building DAG, or calling tools)
The JS CompactionComplete handler in AgentView must only call endCompaction() — it must NOT be reached while DAG construction is in progress
