Codex response.completed has no usage field → stream yields only FinalResponse, no Usage event
Codex response.completed has usage {input:5000, output:2000, total:7000} with no input_tokens_details → Usage has cache_read=None, reasoning=0
Stream yields text deltas followed by Usage then FinalResponse — stream_loop processes Usage event and updates streaming_display before FinalResponse arrives

rules.text: Responses API streaming must yield RawStreamingChoice::Usage before FinalResponse when response.completed contains usage data
Usage event must include input_tokens, output_tokens, total_tokens, cache_read_input_tokens, and reasoning_tokens from the ResponsesUsage struct
The Usage event must be yielded BEFORE the FinalResponse to ensure stream_loop processes it in the correct order
When response.completed has no usage (None), no Usage event should be emitted

examples.text: When work unit moves to SPECIFYING, AI sees reminder: 'Common commands: fspec add-rule <id> "rule" | fspec remove-rule <id> <index> | fspec add-example <id> "example" | fspec remove-example <id> <index> | fspec add-question <id> "@human: question?" | fspec answer-question <id> <index> --answer "..." | fspec generate-scenarios <id>. For more: fspec help discovery'

When work unit moves to TESTING, AI sees reminder: 'Common commands: fspec link-coverage <feature> --scenario "..." --test-file <path> --test-lines <range> | fspec show-coverage <feature> | fspec show-feature <name>. Write tests that map to Gherkin scenarios. For more: fspec link-coverage --help'

When work unit moves to IMPLEMENTING, AI sees reminder: 'Common commands: fspec link-coverage <feature> --scenario "..." --impl-file <path> --impl-lines <lines> | fspec checkpoint <id> <name> | fspec restore-checkpoint <id> <name> | fspec list-checkpoints <id>. Write minimal code to pass tests. For more: fspec checkpoint --help'

When work unit moves to VALIDATING, AI sees reminder: 'Common commands: fspec validate | fspec validate-tags | fspec check | fspec audit-coverage <feature> | npm test | npm run check. Run ALL tests to ensure nothing broke. For more: fspec check --help'
When work unit moves to BACKLOG (deprioritization), no command reminder is shown since backlog is a waiting state with no active work

questions.answer: Every time status changes because context switches between work units, backward movement in ACDD workflow, different conversation sessions, and low cost with high value for always having command context

RIG-001.description:
Master story for replacing the rig-core dependency with a purpose-built LLM abstraction layer.

Motivation:
- We maintain a full patched fork of rig-core (~180+ files) but use only ~10% of it
- The patch adds Anthropic cache token support, OAuth handling, and other customizations to ~5-10 files
- rig-core compiles 20+ unused providers, embeddings/RAG, pipelines, vector stores, MCP, loaders, etc.
- rig is at v0.28, still rapidly evolving — every upstream release risks breaking our patches
- We already have our own provider abstractions (LlmProvider trait, ProviderAdapter, etc.)

Scope:
1. Define custom Tool trait + ToolSet (replacing rig::tool::Tool)
2. Define custom message types (replacing rig::message::Message, UserContent, AssistantContent, etc.)
3. Define CompletionModel trait + streaming response types
4. Implement multi-turn streaming agent loop (replacing rig::agent::Agent)
5. Implement StreamingPromptHook equivalent for compaction/history hooks
6. Migrate Anthropic provider HTTP client (SSE streaming, cache tokens, OAuth, thinking)
7. Migrate OpenAI provider HTTP client (SSE streaming, custom base URL)
8. Migrate Gemini provider HTTP client (SSE streaming, history format)
9. Remove rig-core dependency and patches/ directory
10. Update all tests

Approach: Incremental migration — define own traits, make tools implement both temporarily, swap providers one at a time, then remove rig.
RIG-001.title: Replace rig-core with custom LLM abstraction layer

RIG-002.description:
Define the custom Tool trait, ToolDyn wrapper, ToolSet collection, and ToolDefinition struct that replace rig::tool::*.

The trait interface is nearly identical to rig's — NAME const, Error/Args/Output associated types, definition() and call() async methods. The key difference is removing WasmCompat bounds (we don't target WASM) and simplifying the ToolEmbedding/RAG parts we don't use.

This is the foundation — all 12+ tools (Read, Write, Edit, Bash, Grep, Glob, Ls, AstGrep, AstGrepRefactor, WebSearch, Fspec, Bridge + facade wrappers) must implement this trait.

Approach: Define the new trait alongside rig's. Temporarily make tools implement both via a blanket impl or wrapper. This enables incremental migration.
RIG-002.title: Core trait definitions — Tool, ToolSet, ToolDefinition

These types are used pervasively across codelet-core, codelet-providers, and the streaming display. The key is maintaining API compatibility so the migration in consuming code is mechanical find-and-replace of import paths.

RIG-004.description:
Implement the multi-turn streaming agent loop that replaces rig::agent::Agent.

This is the most complex component — the core loop that:
1. Sends prompt + history + tool definitions to the LLM
2. Streams response chunks via SSE
3. Detects tool_use stop reason in the response
4. Deserializes tool call arguments and dispatches to ToolSet
5. Feeds tool results back as the next user message
6. Repeats until end_turn or max_depth reached
7. Calls hooks before/after each API call (StreamingPromptHook equivalent)
8. Supports CancelSignal for interruption
9. Emits MultiTurnStreamItem variants (text chunks, tool calls, tool results, final response)

Approach: Extract and simplify rig's agent/prompt_request/streaming.rs implementation. Remove WASM compat, enum dispatch, RAG tool selection, and other unused features. Keep only the three-provider streaming loop.

Dependencies: RIG-002 (Tool trait), RIG-003 (Message types)
RIG-004.title: Multi-turn streaming agent loop

RIG-005.description:
Implement direct Anthropic API client replacing rig::providers::anthropic.

This is the most feature-rich provider, requiring:
- POST /v1/messages with streaming (stream: true)
- SSE event parsing (message_start, content_block_start, content_block_delta, content_block_stop, message_delta, message_stop)
- Tool use detection in content blocks (type: tool_use)
- Extended thinking / adaptive thinking support
- Prompt caching with cache_control metadata and ephemeral markers
- Cache token extraction from usage (cache_read_input_tokens, cache_creation_input_tokens) 
- OAuth mode (Authorization: Bearer) vs API key mode (x-api-key)
- Beta headers (prompt-caching, interleaved-thinking, context-1m, claude-code, oauth)
- Model-aware beta header selection (PROV-005)
- Stop reason mapping (tool_use, end_turn, max_tokens)

All of this is currently split between patched rig-core, caching_client.rs, cache_token_extractor.rs, and claude.rs. Consolidation into a single clean client will eliminate the need for the patched fork entirely.

Dependencies: RIG-003 (Message types)
RIG-005.title: Anthropic provider HTTP client with SSE streaming

RIG-006.description:
Implement direct OpenAI API client replacing rig::providers::openai.

Features needed:
- POST /v1/chat/completions with streaming (stream: true)
- SSE event parsing (data: {json} lines, [DONE] sentinel)
- Tool call detection (finish_reason: tool_calls, tool_calls array in delta)
- Custom base URL support via OPENAI_BASE_URL (for vLLM, Ollama, LM Studio)
- URL normalization (ensure /v1 suffix)
- Configurable context window and max output tokens via env vars
- Stop reason mapping
- Usage extraction from stream_options: {include_usage: true}

Simpler than Anthropic — no caching, no OAuth, no thinking. The OpenAI streaming format is well-documented and widely implemented.

Dependencies: RIG-003 (Message types)
RIG-006.title: OpenAI provider HTTP client with SSE streaming

RIG-007.description:
Implement direct Gemini API client replacing rig::providers::gemini.

Features needed:
- POST /v1beta/models/{model}:streamGenerateContent with SSE
- Gemini-specific content format (parts array with text/functionCall/functionResponse)
- Tool declaration format (function_declarations)
- History format conversion (Gemini uses 'user'/'model' roles, requires alternating turns)
- GeminiHistoryHook equivalent (ensure thought signatures, handle continuation)
- Usage extraction from usageMetadata
- Stop reason mapping (STOP, MAX_TOKENS, etc.)

Gemini has the most different API format from the others. The GeminiTurnCompletionFacade and GeminiHistoryHook in codelet-core handle the quirks of Gemini's turn structure.

architectureNotes.text: Tool is wired into all 5 providers' create_rig_agent() — same pattern as SessionSearch: import DeepSearchTool from codelet_tools, add .tool(DeepSearchTool::new(session_id)) to each provider's AgentBuilder chain. Verified locations: claude.rs:530, openai.rs:338, gemini.rs:172, codex/mod.rs:364, zai.rs:247.

AMGR-001 (SessionSearch) provides the foundation for session history access. The implementation pattern: (1) Tool struct in codelet/tools/src/session_search/ with types.rs (SessionSearchAction enum, args, results), handler.rs (per-session handler storage via static RwLock<HashMap<Uuid, Handler>>), reassembly.rs (streaming chunk reconstruction). (2) Handler registered in session_manager.rs via set_session_search_handler(session_id, handler) before agent run, cleaned up after. (3) The handler closure captures project_path AND compaction_trimming: Arc<AtomicBool> — the compaction_trimming flag controls whether Layer 0 trimming (CMPCT-010) is applied to SessionSearch results during agent-controlled compaction. (4) inject_summary (CMPCT-008/009) follows the exact same handler pattern — InjectSummaryTool in codelet/tools/src/inject_summary.rs with set_inject_summary_handler/has_inject_summary_handler. DeepSearch should follow this same module pattern for its tool structure but does NOT need inject_summary (read-only sub-agent).

DeepSearch's SessionSearch handler is created via codelet/napi/src/session_search_handler.rs::create_handler(project_path, compaction_trimming). The project_path comes from the parent session's project context (same as the parent agent's handler). compaction_trimming must be Arc::new(AtomicBool::new(false)) since the ephemeral sub-agent never does compaction. This avoids the NAPI boundary problem since the handler is pure Rust — no ThreadsafeFunction needed.

RLM-001.description: Implement a DeepSearch tool that spawns an ephemeral sub-agent to answer questions over arbitrarily large, user-scoped corpora (files, conversation histories, logs). Based on the RLM paper (MIT CSAIL, arXiv:2512.24601). Key insight: this is NOT a BackgroundSession and NOT a REPL environment — it's a simple tool that builds a rig Agent with scoped read-only tools (Read, Grep, AstGrep, Glob, Ls, Bash) PLUS SessionSearch (from AMGR-001) for conversation history access, injects an RLM-adapted system prompt, calls RigAgent::prompt() (non-streaming, multi-turn), and returns the final answer string as the tool result. ~100-150 lines of core code. Code scoping is first-class: caller specifies paths/globs. Session history is accessible via the sub-agent's SessionSearch tool — no temp file serialization needed. Can use a cheaper model for the sub-agent. No persistence, no UI streaming, no custom stream loop — pure Rust, blocking call from the parent tool execution context.

examples.text: Parent agent calls DeepSearch(query='How is authentication handled?', scope=['src/auth/']) and gets back a text answer synthesized from reading the auth source files
DeepSearch with narrow scope=['codelet/tools/src/read.rs'] only lets the sub-agent read that one file — it can't wander into unrelated code
DeepSearch with scope=['src/'] + max_depth=5 returns partial answer with note that depth limit was reached before exhaustive exploration

Parent agent calls DeepSearch(query='What changed in session 7e0358a4?', scope=['src/auth/']) — the sub-agent uses SessionSearch(action='show', session_id='7e0358a4') to load the conversation, then uses Read/Grep on src/auth/ to correlate what was discussed with what's in the code

Parent agent calls DeepSearch(query='Find all sessions where we discussed compaction strategy') — the sub-agent uses SessionSearch(action='search', query='compaction') to find relevant sessions, then SessionSearch(action='show') to drill into the most relevant ones, building up an answer across multiple sessions

DeepSearch sub-agent's system prompt describes: 'You have SessionSearch to explore conversation history (use recent/search/show actions) and Read/Grep/AstGrep/Glob/Ls/Bash to explore code files scoped to [src/]'. The sub-agent iteratively calls SessionSearch(search) → SessionSearch(show) → Read/Grep, building context before answering

DeepSearch called with no scope and no query returns an error — at minimum a query is required. Scope (code paths) is optional: when omitted, the sub-agent has only SessionSearch for session history exploration. When scope is provided, Read/Grep/AstGrep/Glob/Ls/Bash are guided to those paths via the system prompt

questions.answer: Scope is typed facets, not a flat path list. Code gets paths/globs + git refs (branch, commit range, changed-files-only). Sessions get time range + topic keyword + specific IDs + project filter. Spec artifacts covered by code paths. Each content type has its own natural scoping dimensions that compose together.
questions.text: What granularity levels should scope support? e.g., (1) whole codebase, (2) specific directories, (3) specific files, (4) session history, (5) combined — and should there be a 'guided' mode that narrows scope progressively?

questions.answer: Two-pronged approach: (a) system prompt guardrails describe the code scope (paths/globs) and tell the sub-agent to stay within them, (b) SessionSearch naturally scopes session exploration to the project. For v1, system prompt is sufficient since the sub-agent has no motivation to look elsewhere. For v2, tool-level path restriction can be added as a wrapper
questions.text: How do we prevent the sub-agent from going down the wrong path? Options: (a) system prompt guardrails only, (b) actually restrict tool paths at the tool level, (c) phased search — start broad with Grep, narrow with Read

questions.answer: The sub-agent gets SessionSearch as a native tool — it uses SessionSearch(action='search') for keyword matching across sessions, SessionSearch(action='show') to load full conversations, and SessionSearch(action='recent') for discovery. No pre-processing or serialization needed. SessionSearch already handles blob resolution, streaming chunk reassembly, time filtering, and project scoping internally
questions.text: For session history scope — should the sub-agent get raw messages.jsonl + blobs, or a pre-processed/filtered summary? The session-search.sh script already has context/show/search modes — should the serializer mirror those levels?

questions.answer: Yes — scope is naturally composable. DeepSearch params specify code paths (for Read/Grep/AstGrep), and SessionSearch is always available as a tool. The sub-agent decides how to use each based on the query. Example: DeepSearch(query='How was auth refactored?', scope=['src/auth/']) — sub-agent uses Grep on src/auth/ for current state AND SessionSearch to find sessions discussing the refactor
questions.text: Should scope levels be composable? e.g., DeepSearch(scope={code: ['src/auth/'], sessions: ['7e0358a4'], depth: 'shallow'}) vs DeepSearch(scope={code: ['**/*.rs'], sessions: 'current', depth: 'deep'})

rules.text: DeepSearch is a rig Tool (implements rig::tool::Tool trait) that the parent agent calls like any other tool
DeepSearch scope must support both codebase files AND session history (previous conversation context from ~/.fspec/sessions)
The sub-agent uses RigAgent::prompt() (non-streaming, blocking) — NOT the streaming loop, NOT BackgroundSession
Sub-agent is ephemeral — no persistence, no session resume, no worktree, no NAPI boundary. Fresh Uuid::new_v4() for tool session_id
Must use public provider accessors: provider.client() and provider.model() — private fields rig_client/model_name are inaccessible from outside the provider impl
v1 is Claude-only. Multi-provider support (OpenAI, Gemini, Codex, ZAI) deferred to v2
max_depth must be bounded (default 50, not usize::MAX) to prevent runaway sub-agents
Credentials come from env vars already set by the parent session — sub-agent creates a new ProviderManager which reads them

Session history scope uses SessionSearch tool directly — the sub-agent gets its own SessionSearch instance with a registered handler (via set_session_search_handler). No temp file serialization needed. SessionSearch's native parameters (time range, project filter, keyword search, context turns) replace the custom scope facets from the original design

Scope is two composable dimensions: (a) code scope — paths/globs for Read/Grep/AstGrep/Glob/Ls to explore, (b) session scope — the sub-agent has SessionSearch with full access to recent/search/show actions. The caller specifies code paths in the tool params; session access is always available via SessionSearch. The system prompt describes both scopes to guide the sub-agent's exploration strategy

Two-pronged approach: (a) system prompt guardrails describe the code scope (paths/globs) and tell the sub-agent to stay within them, (b) SessionSearch naturally scopes session exploration to the project. For v1, system prompt is sufficient since the sub-agent has no motivation to look elsewhere. For v2, tool-level path restriction can be added as a wrapper

The sub-agent's SessionSearch handler must be registered (via set_session_search_handler) with a fresh ephemeral session_id before calling RigAgent::prompt(), and cleaned up after — following the same lifecycle pattern as session_manager.rs lines 5378-5384 (register) and 5648-5649 (cleanup)

Sub-agent's SessionSearch handler must be created via create_handler(project_path, Arc::new(AtomicBool::new(false))) — compaction_trimming is always false because the ephemeral sub-agent never performs compaction. The compaction_trimming: Arc<AtomicBool> parameter was added to create_handler in CMPCT-010 and controls whether Layer 0 trimming is applied to SessionSearch results

Scope is naturally composable. DeepSearch params specify code paths (for Read/Grep/AstGrep), and SessionSearch is always available as a tool. The sub-agent decides how to use each based on the query. Example: DeepSearch(query='How was auth refactored?', scope=['src/auth/']) — sub-agent uses Grep on src/auth/ for current state AND SessionSearch to find sessions discussing the refactor
Sub-agent gets read-only search tools plus SessionSearch: Read, Grep, AstGrep, Glob, Ls, Bash, SessionSearch — NO Write, Edit, Bridge, Fspec, WebSearch, ConnectMcp, AstGrepRefactor, inject_summary

architectureNotes.text: Current Implementation: src/utils/scenario-similarity.ts uses Levenshtein distance (character-level edit distance) with 70/30 weighted scoring (title vs steps). Has 7 critical bugs and achieves only 60% accuracy.

Proposed Hybrid Algorithm: Combine 5 algorithms with weighted scoring - Jaro-Winkler (30% - title matching), Token Set Ratio (25% - word reordering), Gherkin Structural (20% - Given/When/Then awareness), Trigram Similarity (15% - fuzzy matching), Jaccard Similarity (10% - keyword overlap). Expected 88% accuracy.

Bug Fixes Required: (1) Division by zero for empty strings/keywords, (2) Strip Gherkin keywords before comparison, (3) Include numbers in keyword regex for technical terms, (4) Fix keyword extraction for match objects, (5) Remove redundant lowercasing, (6) Handle step reordering, (7) Support partial step matching.

Performance: All Phase 1+2 algorithms have no external dependencies and run in O(n*m) time or better. For large codebases (100+ scenarios), consider two-stage matching: (1) Fast keyword filtering, (2) Full similarity only on candidates.

Test Coverage: Must cover empty strings, empty steps, empty keywords, special characters, numbers in terms (OAuth2/SHA256), short titles, reordered steps, partial matches, typos, and performance with 100+ scenarios. See src/commands/__tests__/scenario-deduplication.test.ts

References: (1) spec/attachments/SPEC-003/SIMILARITY_ANALYSIS.md - Bug analysis and test gaps, (2) spec/attachments/SPEC-003/ALGORITHM_ANALYSIS.md - Algorithm comparison and implementation guide, (3) Jaro-Winkler, Token Set Ratio, Trigram algorithms ~200 lines total with no dependencies

TOOL-001.description: Implement a facade pattern for tools that presents provider-specific interfaces while sharing a common implementation. Different LLM providers (Claude, Gemini, OpenAI) expect different tool schemas, names, and parameter formats. This story creates an abstraction layer that maps provider-specific tool calls to shared implementations.

examples.text: Claude web search: provider sends {action: {type: 'search', query: 'rust async'}} → facade maps to InternalParams::Search{query: 'rust async'} → base tool executes search
Gemini web search: provider sends {query: 'rust async'} to 'google_web_search' tool → facade maps to InternalParams::Search{query: 'rust async'} → same base tool executes
Gemini URL fetch: provider sends {prompt: 'https://example.com summarize'} to 'web_fetch' tool → facade extracts URL and maps to InternalParams::OpenPage{url: 'https://example.com'}
Registry lookup: tools_for_provider('gemini') returns [GeminiGoogleWebSearchFacade, GeminiWebFetchFacade, GeminiReadFileFacade, ...] but NOT Claude facades
Tool definition for Gemini: google_web_search sends schema {type: 'object', properties: {query: {type: 'string'}}, required: ['query']} - flat structure, no oneOf
Tool definition for Claude: web_search sends schema with oneOf containing search/open_page/find_in_page action variants - Claude handles complex schemas well

rules.text: Each tool facade MUST implement the ToolFacade trait with provider(), tool_name(), definition(), and map_params() methods
Provider-specific parameters MUST be mapped to internal parameters through the facade before tool execution
A single internal tool MAY have multiple facades for a provider (e.g., Gemini has google_web_search AND web_fetch for our web_search)
Tool definitions MUST use JSON Schema format that the target provider understands (no oneOf for Gemini)

Tool definitions sent to the provider API MUST use the provider's expected schema format, tool names, and parameter structures (e.g., Gemini gets 'google_web_search' with flat {query} schema, not 'web_search' with nested action objects)
Base tool implementations MUST remain unchanged - only facades adapt the interface
ProviderToolRegistry MUST return only facades registered for the requested provider

TOOL-012.description:
The Fspec and Bridge tools intermittently fail with 'handler not configured' because they rely on thread-local 'current session' state to look up handlers. This is fundamentally broken:

1. Thread-local state can be polluted by other sessions
2. The 'current' session concept doesn't survive async boundaries reliably
3. Claude Code CLI doesn't set up thread-local state at all

**Root Cause:**
Tools try to discover their session at call time via `get_current_fspec_session()` instead of knowing it at construction time.

**Solution:**
Tool wrappers should be constructed WITH their session ID. The session_id becomes a field on the wrapper struct, passed to registration functions like `claude_fspec_tool(session_id)`. At call time, the tool uses `self.session_id` directly instead of looking up thread-local state.

This eliminates all reliance on 'current session' thread-local storage and makes session association explicit and deterministic.

examples.text: Session manager creates claude_fspec_tool(session_id) → wrapper stores session_id → call() uses self.session_id → correct handler found
Tool call crosses async boundary → self.session_id still valid → handler lookup succeeds (thread-local would fail)
Two sessions A and B each create their own tool instances → A's tool uses A's handler, B's tool uses B's handler → no cross-contamination

Claude Code CLI scenario: Agent built once at startup → no session context at creation time → Current architecture fails. New architecture: CLI must create session_id UUID before building agent, pass to create_rig_agent().

Watcher session A monitors parent session B: A has its own Fspec tool (session_id=A), B has its own Fspec tool (session_id=B). When A's tool is called, handler for A is used. When B's tool is called, handler for B is used. No confusion possible.

questions.answer: create_rig_agent() signature must change to accept session_id as FIRST parameter since it's required for tool construction. All providers (Claude, Gemini, OpenAI, ZAI) must be updated consistently.

questions.answer: Yes, CURRENT_BRIDGE_SESSION uses global RwLock (line 62 bridge_handler.rs), which is WORSE than thread_local - it can be overwritten by any concurrent session. Both Fspec and Bridge tools have the same architectural problem: session lookup at call time. The fix (session_id at construction) applies identically to both.

Tests and examples can use Uuid::nil() when testing tools that don't need handler routing. The handler must still be registered for the session_id if Fspec tool is used.

TOOL-013.description:
The Bash tool currently inherits its working directory from the parent fspec process. When fspec manages multiple parallel sessions with different git worktrees, each session needs to run commands in its own worktree. Currently, agents must prefix every command with 'cd /path/to/worktree &&' which is error-prone and verbose.

Add an optional 'cwd' parameter to the Bash tool that uses Rust's std::process::Command::current_dir() to set the child process working directory before spawning.

If cwd path does not exist, return an error before executing the command

TOOL-014.description:
Currently only BashTool requires session_id. All other tools (ReadTool, WriteTool, EditTool, GrepTool, GlobTool, LsTool, AstGrepTool, AstGrepRefactorTool, WebSearchTool, FspecTool, BridgeTool) use parameterless new() constructors. This means file operations in isolated sessions may read/write from the wrong directory.

All tools must require session_id in their constructor so they can look up effective_cwd via get_effective_cwd(session_id) and operate in the correct worktree directory for isolated sessions.

The CodexProvider currently registers Claude-style tools (Read, Write, Edit, Bash, Grep, Glob, Ls) but the GPT-5.1-codex model is trained on Codex CLI's native tool names and schemas (shell_command, read_file, list_dir, grep_files, apply_patch, view_image, update_plan). TOOL-016.description:
Create a provider-agnostic unified exec tool that supports PTY session management, following VTCode's architecture. Instead of separate tools per provider, build a single unified tool with action-based dispatch that all providers can use.

The unified exec tool consolidates:
- Shell command execution (run action)
- PTY session creation with yield-and-resume (run with tty=true)
- Interactive stdin writing to live sessions (write action)
- Output polling from running sessions (poll action)
- Session listing (list action)
- Session cleanup (close action)

This replaces the current BashTool's one-shot execution model with a session-aware architecture. Each execution either completes immediately (returning exit_code) or yields control back to the LLM with a session_id for follow-up interaction.

Key components:
- ProcessStore: HashMap of session_id → (child_process, stdin_sender, stdout_buffer) with LRU eviction
- Output buffering with configurable yield_time_ms and max_output_tokens
- Background exit watchers for cleanup
- PTY spawning for interactive sessions (tty=true)
- Pipe-mode for non-interactive commands (default)

Reference: VTCode vtcode-core/src/tools/registry/builtins.rs (unified_exec)
Reference: Codex codex-rs/core/src/unified_exec/process_manager.rs

examples.text: Agent runs 'ls -la' with default settings → process exits immediately → returns exit_code: 0, output: file listing, no session_id (backward compatible with BashTool)
Agent runs 'python3' with tty=true → process stays running → returns session_id: 'abc123', no exit_code, output: Python prompt text
Agent calls write action with session_id='abc123', input='print(42)\n' → returns output: '42\n', session_id still present (process alive)
Agent calls write with input='exit()\n' → Python exits → returns exit_code: 0, no session_id, output includes exit message
Agent calls poll on a running session → returns any new output since last read, session_id still present
Agent calls list action → returns array of active sessions with their session_ids and metadata
Agent calls close with session_id → process is killed, session removed from ProcessStore, returns confirmation
65th process spawned when store is full → LRU eviction kills least recently used session (not in top 8 recent), new process takes its slot
Agent runs ['ls', '-la'] as argv array → execvp-style execution without shell interpretation (no glob expansion)
Agent runs 'sleep 300' with yield_time_ms=2000 → after 2 seconds, returns session_id (process still running), output may be empty
Agent runs command with yield_time_ms=50 → clamped to 250ms minimum, process given at least 250ms to produce output

rules.text: The unified exec tool MUST support five actions: run, write, poll, list, close dispatched via an action parameter
The run action spawns a process (PTY if tty=true, pipe otherwise), collects output for yield_time_ms, and returns exit_code if exited or session_id if still running
The write action sends input bytes to a running session's stdin and polls for output, returning new output plus session status
The poll action checks for new output from a running session without sending input, with a higher minimum wait time (5000ms)
ProcessStore MUST enforce a max of 64 concurrent processes with LRU eviction protecting the 8 most recently used sessions
Yield time MUST be clamped: min 250ms, max 30000ms, default 10000ms; poll/empty-write uses min 5000ms
Output buffer per session MUST be capped at 1 MiB (UNIFIED_EXEC_OUTPUT_MAX_BYTES)
When tty=false (default) and process exits within yield_time_ms, behavior MUST be identical to current BashTool one-shot execution for backward compatibility
Background reaper tasks MUST watch for process exit and clean up ProcessStore entries automatically
The command parameter MUST accept both string (shell command) and array of strings (argv for execvp-style) forms
The tool MUST respect session isolation via effective_cwd lookup (TOOL-014 pattern) for workdir resolution
The tool MUST check commands against the blocklist before execution (same as current BashTool)

userStory.benefit: interactive long-running processes can be controlled across multiple tool calls

TOOL-017.description:
Create a provider-agnostic human-in-the-loop (HITL) tool that allows any LLM to request structured user input mid-turn, following VTCode's architecture.

The tool pauses the agent loop, presents a structured question form to the user via the TUI, and resumes with the user's answers.

Schema:
- questions: Array of 1-3 questions
  - id: String (snake_case) - stable answer identifier
  - header: String (≤12 chars) - short UI label
  - question: String - single-sentence prompt
  - options: Optional array of 2-3 mutually exclusive choices
    - label: String - user-facing label (1-5 words)
    - description: String - one sentence explaining impact

Implementation uses the block-on-oneshot pattern:
1. Handler creates a oneshot channel
2. Sends a pause/input-request event to the TUI
3. Awaits the response (agent loop is suspended)
4. TUI renders a modal/wizard with options + freeform text
5. User responds, oneshot resolves, handler returns answers to LLM

Integrates with existing PauseHandler infrastructure in codelet/tools/src/tool_pause.rs.

Mode-gated: only available when TUI is present and interactive. Returns error in headless/non-interactive mode.

Reference: VTCode vtcode-core/src/tools/request_user_input.rs (declaration)
Reference: VTCode src/agent/runloop/unified/request_user_input/modal.rs (TUI execution)
Reference: Codex codex-rs/core/src/tools/handlers/request_user_input.rs

Agent calls request_user_input in headless mode (no handler registered) → tool immediately returns error message about unavailable session mode
Agent sends question with header 'This Is Too Long' (15 chars) → validation rejects with error about header length exceeding 12 characters
Agent sends question with id 'camelCase' → validation rejects because id must be snake_case
User cancels the modal without answering → tool returns {cancelled: true}
Agent sends 4 questions → validation rejects because maxItems is 3
Agent sends question with 1 option → validation rejects because minItems for options is 2
Agent sends question without options (just freeform) → tool accepts it, TUI shows only freeform input for that question, response has empty selected array and populated other field
set_hitl_handler registers handler for session → has_hitl_handler returns true → clear_all_hitl_handlers removes all → has_hitl_handler returns false

rules.text: The tool MUST accept a questions array (1-3 items) where each question has id (snake_case), header (≤12 chars), question (single sentence), and optional options (2-3 mutually exclusive choices with label and description)
The tool MUST use the per-session handler pattern (like InjectSummaryHandler, SessionSearchHandler, FspecHandler) with a global RwLock<HashMap<Uuid, Handler>> registry
The handler MUST block the tool call (synchronously) until the TUI sends back the user's answers, following the same blocking pattern as pause_for_user
Mode-gated: when no HITL handler is registered for the session (headless/non-interactive), return error 'request_user_input is unavailable in the current session mode'
Response MUST return JSON with answers keyed by question id, each containing selected (array of chosen labels) and optional other (freeform text)
Cancellation MUST return JSON with cancelled: true instead of answers

Validation MUST reject: empty questions array, questions with empty id/header/question, header longer than 12 chars, id not in snake_case, fewer than 2 or more than 3 options per question, more than 3 questions
The tool module MUST live in codelet/tools/src/request_user_input.rs following the established single-file handler pattern (like inject_summary.rs)
The tool MUST NOT depend on PauseHandler - it uses its own separate handler type (HitlHandler) to avoid mixing structured question/answer data with the simple continue/confirm pause semantics
The tool MUST be registered in lib.rs with pub use exports and in facade/mod.rs for facade support

architectureNotes.text: VISUAL MODE: Uses pdfium-render crate (Rust wrapper for Google Pdfium C++ library). Renders pages via PdfPage::render_with_config() at 150 DPI to PdfBitmap, converts to image::DynamicImage, encodes as PNG base64. Returns array of {page_number, data, media_type} objects.

TEXT MODE: Uses lopdf crate (pure Rust). Loads via Document::load_mem(), iterates pages with get_pages(), extracts text with extract_text(&[page_num]). Returns paginated string with '--- Page N ---' separators. Already implemented in pdf.rs.

IMAGES MODE: Uses lopdf crate. Iterates PDF objects looking for XObject streams with /Subtype /Image. Extracts raw image bytes, determines format from /Filter (DCTDecode=JPEG, FlateDecode+decode=PNG). Returns array of {data, media_type, width, height} objects.

ENCRYPTION DETECTION: Check raw bytes for /Encrypt dictionary marker BEFORE lopdf parsing. Also check Document::is_encrypted() after load. Return PdfError::Encrypted early to avoid parsing errors on encrypted content streams.

API DESIGN: ReadArgs gains optional pdf_mode: Option<String> field. Values: 'visual' (default), 'text', 'images'. Invalid values fall back to visual. Output varies by mode: visual/images return JSON array of image objects, text returns paginated string.

DEPENDENCY: pdfium-render requires Pdfium C library. Use pdfium-render with 'static' feature to bundle Pdfium, or 'dynamic' to link at runtime. Consider platform-specific builds (pdfium-render supports Linux, macOS, Windows, WASM).

LLM reads api-spec.pdf with pdf_mode=text to find endpoints → text mode extracts searchable text → LLM locates POST /users endpoint definition
LLM reads flowchart.pdf to understand a business process → visual mode (default) shows the diagram → LLM traces decision paths and explains the flow
LLM reads product-catalog.pdf with pdf_mode=images → images mode extracts 15 embedded product photos → LLM can analyze or describe each product image
LLM reads contract.pdf with pdf_mode=text for legal analysis → all 30 pages extracted as text with page numbers → LLM searches for liability clauses
LLM tries to read encrypted.pdf → encryption detected before parsing → returns error 'Cannot read password-protected PDF: encrypted.pdf'
LLM reads presentation.pdf with slides and charts → visual mode (default) renders each slide → LLM can describe slide content including graphs and diagrams
LLM reads scanned-document.pdf (image-based PDF) → visual mode renders the scanned image → LLM can read text from the rendered image (text mode would return empty)

rules.text: Read tool MUST support three PDF modes via optional pdf_mode parameter: 'visual' (render pages as images), 'text' (extract text), 'images' (extract embedded images)
Default mode MUST be 'visual' because multimodal LLMs can see rendered pages, preserving ALL information (text, layout, diagrams, charts) that text extraction loses
Visual mode MUST render each PDF page as a PNG image at 150 DPI and return as base64-encoded data array with page numbers
Text mode MUST extract text page-by-page with clear page number labels (--- Page N ---), preserving reading order
Images mode MUST iterate PDF XObject streams to extract all embedded images, returning base64 array with media types and dimensions
Password-protected PDFs MUST be detected via /Encrypt dictionary marker in raw bytes BEFORE parsing, returning clear error: 'Cannot read password-protected PDF'
All PDF modes MUST be exempt from text token limits since they return structured content (base64 images or paginated text)
Visual mode SHOULD include page count in output so LLM knows total context being consumed

The TUI should receive events or updates when checkpoints are created or restored, eliminating the need for file system watching.

questions.answer: Use cross-platform IPC (Unix domain sockets on Linux/Mac, named pipes on Windows) via Node.js net module. TUI runs IPC server, checkpoint commands send messages. No event emitter pattern, no polling - direct IPC communication.
questions.text: @human: Should we use an event emitter pattern to notify the TUI of checkpoint changes, or should CheckpointPanel poll for updates at regular intervals?

questions.answer: Updates are asynchronous. IPC messages trigger zustand store loadCheckpointCounts() which updates state asynchronously, causing CheckpointPanel to re-render via React hooks.
questions.text: @human: When checkpoint commands are executed from within the TUI (if that's possible), should updates be synchronous or asynchronous?

questions.answer: Yes, TUI performs initial checkpoint counting on mount by calling useFspecStore.getState().loadCheckpointCounts(). This loads current state from disk. Subsequent updates come from IPC notifications.
questions.text: @human: Should the TUI continue to perform initial checkpoint counting on mount (like current implementation), or should all counts come from command-triggered updates?

questions.answer: IPC solves this. When checkpoint commands execute in another terminal, they send IPC message to TUI's server (net.connect to socket/pipe). If TUI not running, send fails silently. No file-watching needed.
questions.text: @human: If checkpoint commands are executed outside the TUI (in another terminal), how should the TUI detect those changes without file-watching?

TUI-060.description:
Session header displays work unit ID and status with realtime updates using proper Zustand architecture.

## Architecture Requirements

### Source of Truth
- **Rust session state** is the source of truth for session information (model, work unit ID, status)
- **work-units.json** via singleton Rust watcher (notify crate) updates the board display

### Data Flow
1. Rust session state → AgentView sync effect → sessionStore updated
2. work-units.json → Rust file watcher (BoardView ONLY) → fspecStore.loadData()
3. SessionHeader subscribes to sessionStore directly (NO props for dynamic state)

### Key Constraints
- ONE singleton Rust file watcher for work-units.json at BoardView level
- AgentView does NOT create its own watcher
- SessionHeader uses Zustand hooks, not props, for work unit info

TUI-078.description: When mouse tracking (?1000h) is active, the terminal hands all mouse button events to the app, which breaks native text selection. The fix: on button-down events (buttonByte 32-34), temporarily disable mouse tracking so the terminal handles the drag natively, then re-enable on button-release (35) or after a 5000ms fallback timeout. Scroll wheel events (96-99) are unaffected and keep working throughout.

User clicks twice quickly → timer is reset, and mouse tracking stays disabled for the full 5s fallback window from the second click unless button-release re-enables it sooner

rules.text: When ?1000h (X10 mouse tracking) is active, the terminal hands all mouse button events to the app — this prevents native terminal text selection entirely
Mouse button-down events (buttonByte 32–34) and scroll wheel events (96–99) are distinguishable in the ?1000h raw escape sequence at charCodeAt(2)
When a button-down event (32–34) arrives, ?1000l must be written to stdout immediately so the terminal regains control for native click-and-drag selection
Any pending re-enable timer must be cancelled and restarted if a second button-down arrives before the previous timeout fires
On VirtualList unmount or when isFocused becomes false, any pending re-enable timer must be cleared before ?1000l is written
After button-down, ?1000h is re-enabled either when button-release (35) arrives OR after a 5000ms fallback timeout, whichever comes first
Scroll wheel events (96–99) are always handled normally and never trigger ?1000l — the 5000ms fallback window only applies to button-down events

TUI-079.description:
When work-units.json is modified (e.g. by an AI agent changing a work unit status via Fspec tool), the BoardView fails to fully reflect the changes. Work unit ordering within columns is wrong, the last-changed indicator never moves, new attachments don't appear, and deleted work units remain as ghosts. Root cause: TUI-060 moved the file watcher to globalStreamListener which calls updateWorkUnitsFromWatcher() instead of loadData(), losing ordering, stateHistory, attachments, and deletion information.

Additional finding (Gap 8): When the currently-attached work unit is deleted externally, globalStreamListener's session sync logic (lines 68-86) does not clear sessionStore.currentWorkUnitId. The session header continues showing the deleted work unit. This must also be handled — after loadData() completes, if the current work unit no longer exists in the store, session context should be cleared.

Full WorkUnit fields (stateHistory, attachments, updated, etc.) must be available after a watcher-triggered reload — not just the 7 fields from Rust WorkUnitInfo
Work units deleted from work-units.json must be removed from the store after a watcher-triggered reload — no ghost entries

The Rust watcher event serves purely as a file-changed signal — the watcher data (chunk.workUnits) should not be used for store updates or session sync after the fix

architectureNotes.text: Root cause analysis: fspec implementation uses panzoom.zoomToPoint() method which doesn't correctly implement zoom-to-cursor behavior. Mindstrike manually calculates viewport offset using formula: newX = viewport.x + (mouseX - viewport.x) * (1 - zoomRatio). This keeps the point under the cursor fixed during zoom. Current implementation passes clientX/clientY to panzoom but library's zoomToPoint doesn't work as expected.

Trackpad jitter cause: Trackpads send many rapid scroll events with tiny deltaY values. Each event triggers immediate zoom state change. Solution: implement debouncing or accumulate deltas over short time window (e.g., 16ms) before applying zoom. Mindstrike may benefit from ReactFlow's internal smoothing.

Implementation approach: Replace panzoom.zoomToPoint() call with manual viewport calculation matching mindstrike's MindMap.tsx lines 1004-1012. Get panzoom's current pan/zoom state, calculate new state with zoom-to-point formula, then apply with panzoom.zoom() and panzoom.pan() separately.

VIEW-002.description: The fullscreen mermaid diagram viewer zoom feature has two critical issues: 1) Zoom does not zoom FROM the mouse position (should keep point under cursor fixed), 2) Trackpad scrolling causes jitter instead of smooth zoom. The implementation relies on panzoom.zoomToPoint() which doesn't match mindstrike's working manual zoom-to-point formula. Trackpad events need debouncing/smoothing.

questions.answer: Yes, watcher responses have observed_correlation_ids array. The array is populated at breakpoint time (Done, ToolResult, or silence timeout) by capturing correlation IDs from all buffered parent chunks before clearing the buffer. This allows precise tracking of which parent content triggered each watcher response.
questions.text: @human: The architecture doc shows watcher preserving correlationId when wrapping observations, but the watcher doesn't emit Observation chunks to its UI - it emits its own Text responses. Should watcher responses have an observed_correlation_ids array listing which parent chunks triggered them? Or is there a simpler approach?

questions.answer: Chunk-level correlation with turn-level UI aggregation. Each StreamChunk gets its own unique correlation_id assigned by handle_output(). The UI aggregates to turn level by building a map from parent messageIndex to watcher messageIndex using the correlation IDs. This preserves precision in the backend while keeping the UI simple.
questions.text: @human: Should correlation be at chunk level (every Text chunk gets its own ID) or turn level (all chunks in a turn share an ID)? Turn-level seems simpler for UI highlighting since we already group by messageIndex.

questions.answer: Cyan color with bold text and a vertical bar prefix ('│ '). The cross-pane highlighted lines use: color='cyan', bold=true, and prepend '│ ' to content. This is distinct from the active selection (which uses arrow bars ▼▼▼) and clearly visible in the dimmed inactive pane.
questions.text: @human: What visual style for cross-pane highlight? Options: cyan background on the line, a vertical bar/marker on the left edge, or dimmed/brightened text? The active selection already uses arrow bars (▼▼▼), so this should be visually distinct.

WATCH-024.description: Rename the entire watcher system terminology from parent/watcher to subordinate/supervisor, replace WatchGraph with ChainOfCommand, and remove the RoleAuthority enum. A subordinate is the session doing the work. A supervisor observes and interjects. The brief field provides all the behavioral instruction — no artificial authority levels needed. Relationships are dynamic (can change at any time) and a subordinate can have multiple supervisors. This is a pure refactoring — no new functionality, just clearer naming that matches the actual architecture.
